candidates.name: Surface coating of plastic parts and products

criteria.check: Whether the solvent-welding step is an application of a 'surface coating' to a substrate (i.e., an application of a material to a part, including associated activities such as surface preparation or cleaning) as defined in §63.4481(a)(1).

Whether the material applied (methylene chloride or a formulation containing it) is a 'coating' or an 'adhesive/adhesive coating' (a chemical substance applied for the purpose of bonding two surfaces) as defined in §63.4581.

Whether the affected source uses 378 liters (100 gallons) per year or more of coatings that contain HAP in the surface coating of plastic parts and products and is a major source (or located at/part of a major source) as required by §63.4481(b).

Whether the solvent-welding lines and their associated storage, mixing, conveyance, and waste-handling equipment fall within the affected source definition for surface coating of plastic parts and products in §63.4482(b).

you_should_check: Is the methylene-chloride application performed specifically to bond plastic parts (i.e., functioning as an adhesive) versus solely as a cleaning/degreasing step?
How the material is classified by the supplier/manufacturer (coating/adhesive vs. cleaning solvent) and manufacturer's formulation data showing organic HAP content and solids.
Annual volume (liters or gallons per year) of the HAP-containing material used in these solvent-welding lines (include the six new lines in the projection).
Confirm facility major-source status for HAP (single HAP ≥10 tpy or combined HAP ≥25 tpy) and that the parts being treated are plastic parts/products (e.g., medical device plastic components).

candidates.name: Secondary Copper Smelters (area source)

criteria.check: Determine whether the facility is a “secondary copper smelter,” i.e., it processes copper scrap in a blast furnace and converter or uses another pyrometallurgical purification process to produce anode copper from copper scrap.
Determine whether the product is “anode copper,” i.e., copper cast into anodes and refined in an electrolytic process (if yes, that supports classification as a secondary copper smelter).
Confirm the source is an area source of HAPs (the subpart applies to an area source secondary copper smelter).
Confirm whether the secondary copper smelter is a new affected source (constructed or reconstructed on or after October 6, 2006), since the subpart applies to each new affected source.

you_should_check: Does the plant’s process qualify as pyrometallurgical purification of scrap (oxidation/reduction, fluxing, smelting steps) versus merely melting scrap to make ingots or feedstock for onsite manufacture?
Is the product you cast shipped as anodes for electrolytic refining (i.e., anode copper)?
Is the permitted/title status of the facility an HAP area source (synthetic minor) under state/federal permits?
What is the date of construction/startup or reconstruction relative to October 6, 2006?

candidates.name: Perchloroethylene (PCE) Dry Cleaning (NESHAP Subpart M)

criteria.check: Whether the facility is a dry cleaning facility that uses perchloroethylene (PCE).

Whether, after December 21, 2020, the requirement to eliminate any emission of PCE applies to any dry cleaning system that is located in a building with a residence (i.e., whether the machine is located in a building with a residence).

Whether the apartment above the shop qualifies as a 'residence' under the definition in §63.321 and whether vacancy affects that status (§63.324(f)(3) requires reporting if located in a building with a residence even if the residence is vacant).
The construction/reconstruction date of the dry cleaning system to determine if it falls into the §63.320(b)(2)(ii) cohort (systems with special compliance provisions listed in §63.322(o)(5)(ii)).

you_should_check: Do you use perchloroethylene (PCE) at this shop?
Is the dry cleaning machine located in the same building as the upstairs apartment (i.e., in a building that contains a residence)?
Does the upstairs apartment meet the definition of 'residence' (not short-term <180 days) and is it currently vacant?
What is the original construction or reconstruction date of the dry cleaning machine/system (to see if §63.320(b)(2)(ii) / §63.322(o)(5)(ii) apply)

candidates.name: Area-source Metal Fabrication and Finishing NESHAP

criteria.check: Do you own or operate an area source that is primarily engaged in operations in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in §63.11514(a)(1)–(9)?
Is at least 50 percent of facility production (using the previous continuous 12 months) in one of those nine source categories (i.e., does the facility meet the 'primarily engaged' definition)?

Does the facility use materials that contain MFHAP (cadmium, chromium, lead, or nickel ≥ 0.1% by weight, or manganese ≥ 1.0% by weight as shown by manufacturer/supplier formulation data or MSDS) or have the potential to emit MFHAP?

Does the facility perform any of the affected-source activities listed (dry abrasive blasting, machining, dry grinding/dry polishing with machines, spray painting, or welding) on materials that contain or could emit MFHAP?

you_should_check: Whether the facility is an area source (and not a major source) under applicable definitions.

The previous continuous 12 months' production mix to confirm ≥50% production within one of the nine listed categories (e.g., Electrical and Electronic Equipment Finishing or Fabricated Metal Products).
Which specific processes are performed on-site (dry abrasive blasting, machining, dry grinding/polishing with machines, spray painting, welding).
Material formulation/MSDS data showing metal content (wt% of Cd, Cr, Pb, Ni, Mn) to determine if materials contain MFHAP above the thresholds in §63.11514(b).

candidates.name: Lime manufacturing plants

criteria.check: Whether you own or operate a lime manufacturing plant (LMP) that is a major source or is located at, or part of, a major source of HAP emissions.
Whether the establishment manufactures lime product by calcination of limestone, dolomite, shells, or other calcareous substances (i.e., whether the kiln produces a lime product).
Whether the plant site is a major source of HAP (any single HAP ≥ 9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or any combination of HAP ≥ 22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy)).

Whether the specific lime kiln (and any associated cooler or processed stone handling operations) is located at an LMP that is a major source, because this subpart applies to those units at an LMP that is a major source.

you_should_check: Does the kiln produce a lime product by calcining calcareous material (e.g., lime mud) rather than only regenerating/reusing an internal byproduct without producing a lime product for reuse/sale?
Is the plant site a major source by current actual or potential HAP emissions (compare totals to 10 tpy single / 25 tpy combined thresholds)?
Is the plant located at one of the listed excluded facility types (kraft pulp mill, soda pulp mill, sulfite pulp mill, beet sugar plant, or only processes water‑softening sludge)?
If relevant to which limits apply, confirm whether the kiln is 'new' or 'existing' based on your construction/reconstruction dates (see applicability timing in §63.7082).

candidates.name: Stationary RICE (reciprocating internal combustion engines)

criteria.check: Whether the engines are existing non‑emergency 4SLB or 4SRB stationary RICE with a site rating of more than 500 HP located at an area source of HAP (if yes, the paragraph’s initial compliance provisions apply).
Whether each engine meets the definitions of four‑stroke and lean‑burn (to confirm the 4SLB/4SRB classification used in the applicability language).
Whether the engines are remote stationary RICE (the performance‑test requirement in this paragraph applies only to engines that are not remote).
Whether each engine is operated more than 24 hours per calendar year (the initial performance‑test provisions apply only to units operated >24 hours/yr).

you_should_check: engine model/type and confirm four‑stroke lean‑burn classification
site rating (horsepower) for each engine (800 hp stated)
facility major vs area‑source status (you stated area source)
annual operating hours per engine (>24 hr/yr vs ≤24 hr/yr)
whether you have established and documented remote status (geographic criteria) and the date it was met

candidates.name: General Provisions (notifications)

criteria.check: Whether you submitted the initial notification required when the affected source became subject to the standard (not later than 120 calendar days after becoming subject).
Whether you are required to submit the notifications listed in §63.6645 because you own or operate existing stationary RICE located at an area source of HAP emissions.
Whether you submitted a Notification of Intent to conduct a performance test at least 60 calendar days before any scheduled performance test.

Whether you submitted a Notification of Compliance Status within the required period (e.g., before the close of business on the 60th day following completion of the performance test or other initial compliance demonstration).

you_should_check: whether an initial notification was submitted and the submittal date
whether a 60‑day Notification of Intent to test was submitted for any performance test
whether a Notification of Compliance Status was submitted within the required post‑test deadline
whether notifications were sent to the appropriate recipient (State or EPA Regional Office) per §63.9(a)(4)

candidates.name: Gasoline Dispensing Facilities (GDF) NESHAP

criteria.check: Whether the affected source is a gasoline dispensing facility (GDF) that is located at an area source, since this subpart applies to each GDF at an area source.

Whether the tanks are part of a GDF as defined (a stationary facility that dispenses gasoline into the fuel tank of a motor vehicle, motor vehicle engine, nonroad vehicle, or nonroad engine, including on‑site company vehicles).

Whether the liquid in each tank meets the definition of 'gasoline' (a petroleum distillate or distillate/alcohol blend with Reid vapor pressure ≥27.6 kPa and used as a fuel for internal combustion engines), to distinguish gasoline tanks from diesel tanks.
What the GDF monthly gasoline throughput is (if <10,000 gallons/month then the applicable requirements are in §63.11116; higher tiers are addressed in §63.11111(b)–(d)).

you_should_check: Confirm the site is an EPA/CAA ‘area source’ (you stated it is an area source).
Confirm each tank’s contents and Reid vapor pressure to identify which tanks are ‘gasoline’ per §63.11132.
Confirm that dispensing to company vehicles constitutes dispensing into motor vehicle fuel tanks at the stationary facility (i.e., meets the GDF definition).
Calculate monthly throughput for all gasoline storage tanks at that single GDF (sum of current day + previous 364 days ÷ 12 per §63.11111(h))

candidates.name: Area‑Source Bulk Gasoline Distribution NESHAP

criteria.check: Whether you own or operate one or more affected area sources identified (a bulk gasoline terminal not subject to subparts R/CC, a pipeline breakout station, a pipeline pumping station, or a bulk gasoline plant).

Whether the gasoline storage tanks are used only for dispensing gasoline in a manner consistent with tanks at a GDF—if so, those tanks are not subject to this subpart and must comply with subpart CCCCCC instead.

Whether the facility meets applicable throughput/design‑capacity thresholds for bulk gasoline plants or terminals (exceeding thresholds can make the affected source subject to this subpart and can continue to subject it even if throughput later drops).

you_should_check: Confirm whether the site is a bulk gasoline terminal, pipeline breakout station, pipeline pumping station, or bulk gasoline plant (type of operation and how gasoline is received/redistributed).
Confirm applicable throughput or design capacity metrics for the facility to see if bulk‑facility thresholds are met.
Confirm whether the storage tanks in question are used only for dispensing consistent with a GDF (if yes, follow subpart CCCCCC per §63.11081(c)).

candidates.name: Portland cement plants (Subpart LLL)

criteria.check: Determine whether the facility is a portland cement plant that is a major source or an area source (this subpart applies only to new and existing portland cement plants that are major or area sources).
Determine whether the coal mill is an inline coal mill associated with a kiln (the affected sources include each kiln including inline coal mills).

If the inline coal mill exhausts through a separate stack or is otherwise associated with the kiln, the combined PM emissions from the kiln and the alkali bypass and/or inline coal mill stack are subject to the PM emissions limit in this subpart (and alternative PM limits apply when exhausts are combined into a single stream).

PM compliance requires Method 5 or 5I performance testing and establishment/use of a PM CPMS with a site‑specific operating limit (annual performance tests and continuous PM CPMS monitoring on a 30 operating‑day rolling average; when coal mill has a separate stack, test kiln and coal mill simultaneously and compute combined PM as required).

you_should_check: Is the plant classified as a major source or an area source under §63.2?
Is the coal mill an inline coal mill that receives/diverts kiln exhaust and is it exhausted via its own stack?
Is the kiln existing or new (to identify the numeric PM limit in Table 1 of §63.1343)?
Do you have/will you perform Method 5/5I testing and install/operate a PM CPMS and perform the required annual and 30‑day rolling average monitoring?

candidates.name: Secondary Aluminum Production (NESHAP Subpart RRR)

criteria.check: Determine whether your plant is a 'secondary aluminum production facility' (see §63.1503), because this subpart applies to owners/operators of such facilities.

If the facility is a major source of HAPs, determine whether the delamination chambers are an affected source listed as a 'scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln' (each new and existing unit listed applies at major sources).

Determine whether the delamination chambers meet the definition of 'scrap dryer/delacquering kiln/decoating kiln' — i.e., a unit used primarily to remove organic contaminants (oil, paint, lacquer, ink, plastic, and/or rubber) from aluminum scrap prior to melting, or to separate aluminum foil from paper and plastic in scrap.

If the facility is an area source of HAPs rather than a major source, determine whether the delamination units are subject to the D/F-related provisions because scrap dryers/delacquering kilns/decoating kilns are listed for area-source D/F requirements.

you_should_check: Whether your plant qualifies as a 'secondary aluminum production facility' under §63.1503
Whether the delamination chambers are used primarily to remove paint/plastic (organic contaminants) or to separate foil from scrap
Whether the delamination units operate 'prior to melting' of that scrap (per the definition language)
Whether the facility is a major source or an area source of HAPs (to know which parts of Subpart RRR apply)

candidates.name: Paint stripping and motor vehicle/mobile equipment surface coating (area-source NESHAP)

criteria.check: Whether the facility is an area source of HAP (i.e., not a major source, not located at or part of a major source).
Whether you perform paint stripping using methylene chloride (MeCl) for removal of dried paint (this activity is covered by the subpart).

Whether you perform spray application of coatings to motor vehicles or mobile equipment (autobody refinishing) at a fixed location or as mobile repair/refinishing — such operations are covered by the subpart unless an exemption applies).

Whether you spray apply any coatings that contain the target HAP (Cr, Pb, Mn, Ni, Cd); if you spray apply no target-HAP-containing coatings you may petition or (on/after May 9, 2023) submit a notification to the Administrator claiming that you do not spray apply target-HAP coatings and must retain supporting records and certification.

Confirm whether any spray-applied refinish coatings contain target HAP (supplier data sheets, formulations, and your certification)

Confirm whether you perform spray application to motor vehicles/mobile equipment at your location (number of booths/painters) and whether you will submit the notification/petition and retain required records

candidates.name: Area-source Paint Stripping and Surface Coating NESHAP

criteria.check: Confirm the facility is an area source of HAP (not a major source as defined by the single-HAP 10 Mg/yr (10 tpy) or combined-HAP 25 tpy thresholds).

Determine whether you perform spray application of coatings that contain the target HAP (compounds of Cr, Pb, Mn, Ni, or Cd) to any part or product made of metal or plastic (excluding facility maintenance or space vehicles).

Verify whether the coatings used (including the polyurea) contain any individual target HAP above the subpart thresholds (greater than 0.1% by mass for carcinogenic target HAP or greater than 1.0% by mass for other individual target HAP).

Confirm whether the polyurea spray line is part of the affected source (i.e., is included within the collection of equipment such as spray booths, spray guns, mixing rooms, and cleaning equipment that comprise the affected source).

you_should_check: Facility-wide potential and actual HAP emissions to confirm area-source vs major-source status (compare to 10 tpy single / 25 tpy combined thresholds).
Coating formulation documentation (SDS, supplier specs) for the polyurea line and other lines to confirm presence/absence and concentrations of target HAP (Cr, Pb, Mn, Ni, Cd).
Whether the polyurea operation is spray application to metal/plastic parts (not facility maintenance or another excluded activity).
Whether the polyurea line is grouped with other surface-coating equipment at the facility such that it is included in the affected source per §63.11171(b).

candidates.name: Stationary combustion turbines

criteria.check: Determine whether this unit is a new or reconstructed lean premix gas‑fired stationary combustion turbine that must comply with the emission and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2.

If the turbine is not equipped with an oxidation catalyst, you must petition the Administrator for operating limitations (or for approval of no additional operating limitations) to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation, and you must measure the petitioned operating parameters during the initial performance test and continuously thereafter.

Your petition must identify the specific parameters you propose (e.g., turbine speed, inlet air temperature), discuss how those parameters affect HAP emissions and how limits will control HAPs, explain how you will set upper/lower parameter values, describe measurement and monitoring methods and instruments (including accuracy/precision), and describe recalibration frequency and methods.

Submit a notification of intent to conduct the initial performance test at least 60 days before the test, and submit the Notification of Compliance Status including performance test results within 60 calendar days after completion of each performance test.

Determine whether an initial performance test is required (and whether any prior acceptable test exists per 63.6110), schedule the test, submit the 60‑day advance notice, and plan to submit the Notification of Compliance Status within 60 days after the test.

candidates.name: Metal fabrication & finishing area-source NESHAP

criteria.check: Whether the facility is an area source that is primarily engaged (see §63.11522) in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in §63.11514(a).
What 'primarily engaged' means (≥50% of facility production from one of the listed source categories, measured over the previous continuous 12 months) (definition in §63.11522).

Whether the facility performs any affected source activities (dry abrasive blasting, machining, dry grinding/polishing, spray painting, or welding) that use materials that contain or have the potential to emit MFHAP as defined in §63.11514(b) and §63.11522 (metal and concentration thresholds).

Whether the current repair activities qualify as excluded 'tool or equipment repair operations, facility maintenance, or quality control activities' per §63.11514(f) and the definitions in §63.11522 (if so, the subpart does not apply).

you_should_check: Confirm whether your facility's primary NAICS/SIC activity (ship building/repair SIC 3731, NAICS 336611) corresponds to one of the nine source categories in §63.11514(a) and document the 12‑month production basis used to determine 'primarily engaged' per §63.11522.
Inventory all processes (dry abrasive blasting, welding, spray painting, machining, dry grinding/polishing) actually performed on site and identify which are included in §63.11514(b)(1)–(5).

For each paint, solvent, abrasive, base metal, and consumable, check MSDS/formulation data against MFHAP thresholds in §63.11514(b) and the 'material containing MFHAP' definition in §63.11522 to see if MFHAP are present or there is potential to emit.

Determine whether the current work is customer-oriented ship repair/maintenance (potentially 'tool or equipment repair' or 'facility maintenance' exclusions) versus manufacture/fabrication of products as described in §63.11514(f) and the definitions in §63.11522.

candidates.name: Area-source metal fabrication and finishing

criteria.check: Determine whether your area source is primarily engaged in operations in one of the nine metal fabrication and finishing source categories listed in §63.11514(a)(1)–(9) (see Table 1 descriptions).

Determine whether your facility is 'primarily engaged' as defined in §63.11522, i.e., production of products in a listed category represents at least 50 percent of facility production over the previous continuous 12 months (use volume, linear foot, square foot, or other industry-appropriate measure).

Determine whether you perform metal fabrication or finishing operations as defined in §63.11522 (dry abrasive blasting, machining, dry grinding and polishing with machines, spray-applied painting, or welding).

Determine whether the materials used in those operations contain or have the potential to emit MFHAP (cadmium, chromium, lead, manganese, nickel) at or above the thresholds in §63.11514(b) (Cd/Cr/Pb/Ni ≥0.1% by weight; Mn ≥1.0% by weight).

you_should_check: What products you manufacture/assemble and whether those products match any category descriptions in Table 1 (identify which Table‑1 category, if any).

The percentage of facility production (by an appropriate unit) over the past continuous 12 months that is production of the Table‑1 product(s) to confirm the ≥50% 'primarily engaged' test (document calculations).

Which specific operations you perform (confirm dry machining, dry grinding, dry abrasive blasting, spray painting, welding) and the fraction/number of pumps undergoing those finishing steps (e.g., exact percent < or ≥50%).

MSDS/formulation data for base metals, paints, abrasives, and other materials to confirm MFHAP content against the thresholds, and whether the processes have the potential to emit MFHAP; also confirm whether activities are repair/maintenance/quality‑control (see §63.11514(f) and definitions in §63.11522) which may affect applicability.

candidates.name: Stationary RICE NESHAP (Subpart ZZZZ)

criteria.check: Determine whether each engine is a stationary RICE (i.e., an internal combustion engine that is not mobile, is not a non‑road engine as defined at 40 CFR 1068.30, and is not used to propel a motor vehicle).
Determine whether your plant is a major source (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP) or an area source, because applicability is to stationary RICE at major or area sources.

Determine whether each engine meets the Emergency stationary RICE definition (operated to provide power/mechanical work during emergencies and meets the operating limits in §63.6640(f)), since emergency engines may be treated differently under this subpart.
Determine whether each engine is existing, new, or reconstructed and its site rating (brake HP) because different compliance categories and dates apply based on construction date and HP.

you_should_check: Is each diesel engine fixed in place or designated/registered as a non‑road/portable engine (per 40 CFR 1068.30)?
Total plant HAP actual and potential emissions (tons/year) to classify major vs area source.
Whether the engines are operated for emergency use only and meet §63.6640(f) conditions.
Engine site rating (brake HP) and construction/startup or reconstruction date for each engine.

candidates.name: NSPS for Stationary RICE (may preclude further Part 63 requirements)

criteria.check: If the engine is new or reconstructed and located at an area source, check whether it must meet 40 CFR part 60 subpart IIII (CI) or JJJJ (SI) instead of Subpart ZZZZ.

If the engine is a new or reconstructed compression‑ignition (diesel) stationary RICE with site rating ≤500 HP located at a major source, check whether it must meet 40 CFR part 60 subpart IIII instead of Subpart ZZZZ.

If the engine is a new or reconstructed emergency or limited‑use stationary RICE with site rating ≤500 HP located at a major source, check whether it must meet 40 CFR part 60 subpart IIII or JJJJ instead of Subpart ZZZZ.

you_should_check: Was each engine constructed or reconstructed as 'new' on/after the applicable dates (i.e., determine new vs existing per §63.6590(a))?
Engine type: compression‑ignition (diesel) vs spark‑ignition.
Engine site rating (brake HP) to see if ≤500 HP threshold applies.
Whether the engine is located at an area source or major source.

candidates.name: Engine test cells/stands NESHAP

criteria.check: Whether the apparatus you operate is an 'engine test cell/stand' located at a major source of HAP emissions (subject if both true).
Whether the engines tested are 'uninstalled engines' (i.e., not installed in or an integrated part of the final product).

Whether the affected source is 'existing' (construction commenced on or before May 14, 2002) or 'new/reconstructed' (construction/reconstruction commenced after May 14, 2002), because existing affected sources do not have to meet the subpart's requirements.

For new or reconstructed affected sources, whether the source is used in whole or in part for testing internal combustion engines with rated power ≥25 hp, since emission limitations apply to such sources at major sources.

you_should_check: Is your plant a major source of HAPs (any single HAP ≥10 tons/yr or any combination ≥25 tons/yr) per 63.9285(c)?
Are the diesel truck engines being tested 'uninstalled' (not part of the final product) per 63.9375 definition?

When was the engine test cell/stand (affected source) constructed or reconstructed — on or before May 14, 2002, or after — to determine existing vs new/reconstructed status per 63.9290(a)(1)-(3) and (b)?
Are the engines/internal combustion devices being tested rated ≥25 hp and is the affected source used (in whole or in part) to test them per 63.9300?

candidates.name: Utility Mercury and Air Toxics (EGU)

criteria.check: Determine whether you own or operate a coal-fired EGU or an oil-fired EGU as defined in §63.10042.
Confirm the unit meets the EGU definition (a fossil fuel-fired combustion unit of more than 25 MWe that serves a generator that produces electricity for sale).

For oil-fired status, check whether the unit burned oil for more than 10.0 percent of the average annual heat input during the 3 previous calendar years or more than 15.0 percent of the annual heat input during any one of those calendar years.

If the unit is not a coal- or oil-fired EGU, verify whether it meets the natural gas-fired EGU definition or whether it is capable of combusting >25 MWe of oil/coal but did not fire sufficient oil/coal to meet the percentage thresholds (which would exclude it from this subpart).

you_should_check: Unit nameplate or permitted electric output (MWe)
Whether the unit sells electricity for sale
Fuel heat-input fractions: 3-year average oil heat input (%) and any single-year oil heat input (%)
Permitted/actual capability to combust oil or coal (fuel handling, permit allowances)

criteria.check: Determine whether the unit is an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater located at or part of a major source of HAP (per §63.7575 and the major source definition referenced in §63.7485).

Check whether the unit is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) covered by subpart UUUUU or is a natural gas-fired EGU firing at least 85 percent natural gas on an annual heat input basis — either condition would make it not subject to this subpart.
If you are claiming the unit is a natural gas-fired EGU (and thus excluded), confirm the annual heat-input fraction of natural gas (is it ≥85%?).

you_should_check: Whether the boiler is classified as industrial/commercial/institutional versus an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU)
Whether the facility is a major source of HAP
Annual fuel heat-input fractions (natural gas vs. oil) and whether natural gas is ≥85% on an annual basis
Whether the unit is already subject to or excluded by subpart UUUUU

candidates.name: Pesticide Active Ingredient (PAI) MACT

criteria.check: Whether the affected source is the facility‑wide collection of pesticide active ingredient (PAI) manufacturing process units that process, use, or produce HAP and is located at a plant site that is a major source.
Whether the new distillation column is a 'unit operation' (e.g., a distillation unit) that is part of a PAI process unit.
Whether the construction of the affected source (or this addition) commenced after November 10, 1997 (which would define it as a new affected source).

If the distillation would be a dedicated PAI process unit, whether its potential to emit is ≥10 tons/yr of any one HAP or ≥25 tons/yr of combined HAP (which makes it a new dedicated PAI unit subject to new‑source provisions).

Whether the existing raw‑material storage tanks in the neighboring building are part of a PAI process unit (i.e., whether input to or output from the tank to the PAI process unit is ≥ any other input/output to/from that tank).

you_should_check: Is the plant a major source for HAP emissions?
Will the distillation operate as part of the PAI (2,4‑D) manufacturing process (serve the herbicide unit) or as a separate/dedicated non‑PAI unit?
When did onsite construction/installation start (dates) for the column/equipment?
Quantify potential to emit (tpy) of single and combined HAP from the distillation to determine dedicated‑unit status; determine which storage tanks are assigned to the PAI process per §63.1360(f).

candidates.name: Miscellaneous Organic Chemical Manufacturing (MCPU) MACT

criteria.check: Whether you own or operate miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process units (MCPU) that are located at or are part of a major source of HAP.

Whether the unit produces materials described in paragraph (b)(1) (i.e., organic chemicals classified under the listed 1987 SIC codes or 1997 NAICS code 325, or the specific listed compounds/families).

Whether the MCPU processes, uses, or generates any of the organic HAP listed in section 112(b) of the CAA or hydrogen halide/halogen HAP as defined in §63.2550 (i.e., whether HAP are involved in the process or feedstock).
Whether the MCPU (or its process vents) is already an affected source or part of an affected source under another subpart of part 63 (because if so, the MCPU provisions in this subpart do not apply).

you_should_check: Does the distillation and associated equipment form part of an MCPU that produces materials falling under the listed SIC/NAICS codes (confirm NAICS/SIC classification for 2,4‑D operations)?
Does the distillation process process, use, or emit listed organic HAP or hydrogen halide/halogen HAP?
Is the distillation/associated storage already assigned to or regulated under another Part 63 subpart (e.g., the PAI subpart MMM)?

Whether materials in the operation are 'target HAP-containing' — specifically whether nickel compounds are present at ≥0.1 percent by weight (as the metal) in the materials processed, per supplier formulation/SDS data.
Whether the equipment is used for research and development (R&D) versus commercial manufacture, since R&D equipment as defined may be excluded.

criteria.check: Whether the facility performs paints and allied products manufacturing and is an area source that processes, uses, or generates materials containing HAP (i.e., the facility meets the basic applicability in §63.11599(a)).
Whether you add dry pigments or solids that contain nickel to a process vessel or to a grinding/milling process (the rule requires capture during addition of such dry nickel-containing solids).

Whether particulate emissions during the addition of nickel-containing pigments/solids are captured and routed to a particulate control device, or whether the pigments/solids are instead in paste, slurry, or liquid form (which the standard treats differently).

Whether grinding and milling of materials containing nickel occurs (if so, check whether you capture and route particulates to a control device, fully enclose the equipment, or keep pigments/solids in solution as allowed options).

Whether nickel-containing active material is added as a dry powder vs. slurry/paste/liquid

What particulate capture/control measures (hoods, control device, enclosure) are or will be used during additions/grinding

Whether the operation qualifies as a CMPU (all process vessels, equipment, and activities necessary to operate a chemical manufacturing process producing NAICS code 325 materials, including associated storage and transfer operations).
Whether the operation is part of Manufacture of Paint and Allied Products subject to subpart CCCCCCC, because such operations are excluded from subpart VVVVVV per this paragraph.

Confirm facility area-source status

candidates.name: Secondary Aluminum NESHAP (thermal chip dryers)

criteria.check: Whether your site is a 'secondary aluminum production facility' as defined in §63.1503 (the subpart applies only to owners/operators of such facilities).

Whether the unit you will install is a 'thermal chip dryer' (thermal chip dryers are listed as affected sources at secondary aluminum production facilities at major sources (§63.1500(b)(2)) and are listed for D/F requirements at area sources (§63.1500(c)(1))).

If the facility is a major source the thermal chip dryer is subject to the THC limit (0.40 kg THC per Mg feed/charge) and to the D/F limit (2.50 µg D/F TEQ per Mg); if the facility is an area source the thermal chip dryer is subject to the D/F limit (2.50 µg D/F TEQ per Mg).

If the unit is an affected thermal chip dryer you must (a) conduct a performance test measuring THC and D/F at the control device outlet while the unit processes only unpainted aluminum chips (§63.1512(b)), and (b) if emissions are controlled by an afterburner, comply with the thermal chip dryer monitoring requirements (record materials charged and submit required certifications) in §63.1510(k).

you_should_check: Whether your plant meets the definition of a secondary aluminum production facility in §63.1503.
Whether the facility is a major source of HAPs or an area source (determine major/area status).
Whether the new unit qualifies as a 'thermal chip dryer' (how it will be operated and what material is charged).
Whether the dryer will have an afterburner or other control and whether you can perform the required performance test using only unpainted chips.

candidates.name: Utility MACT (Hg and Air Toxics)

criteria.check: Determine whether each boiler is an 'electric utility steam generating unit (EGU)' (fossil fuel-fired unit capable of producing >25 MWe that serves a generator producing electricity for sale).

Confirm the unit is not excluded from this subpart (e.g., it is not a natural gas‑fired EGU under 63.9983(b) and it did not fail the coal/oil-fired fuel‑use thresholds described in 63.10042 as noted in 63.9983(c)).

If the unit is a coal‑fired, liquid oil‑fired, or solid oil‑derived fuel‑fired EGU, check that startup/shutdown operations are governed by the work practice requirements in Table 3 (i.e., emission limits apply at all times except during startup/shutdown, but those EGUs must meet Table 3 work practices during startup/shutdown).

Decide whether the period of firing only to produce auxiliary steam (without generating electricity) meets the regulatory definition of 'startup' in §63.10042 (and if you rely on paragraph (2) of that definition, follow the additional startup/shutdown recording requirements in 63.10020(e)).

you_should_check: Nameplate electrical capacity and whether each boiler serves a generator that produces electricity for sale (to assess EGU status).
Historic fuel use (percent oil, coal, gas) over the prior years used for applicability determinations (to determine oil‑fired EGU status and fuel‑use thresholds).
Permit language and onsite fuel‑handling capability authorizing the fuels (to confirm 'fossil fuel‑fired' capability per 63.10042).

Whether the specific auxiliary‑steam‑only operation fits the regulatory 'startup' definition in §63.10042 and whether you intend to rely on paragraph (2) of that definition (triggering the recordkeeping in 63.10020(e)).

candidates.name: Mercury and Air Toxics Standards (EGUs)

criteria.check: Determine whether the unit is an Electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) — i.e., a fossil fuel-fired combustion unit that serves a generator producing electricity for sale and meets the >25 MWe capability criteria.

Verify whether the unit fired sufficient oil historically to meet the oil-fired EGU definition in §63.10042, because a unit capable of combusting >25 MW that did not fire sufficient oil may not be subject to this subpart.

Calculate the capacity factor for a liquid oil-fired EGU as: (total annual heat input from oil) ÷ (maximum hourly heat input regardless of fuel × 8,760 hours) to be used in assessing limited‑use status.

Check whether the unit 'qualifies as a limited‑use liquid oil‑fired' as defined in §63.10042, because limited‑use liquid oil‑fired EGUs are not subject to the emission limits in Tables 1 and 2 and instead must meet the tune‑up work practice in Table 3.

you_should_check: Unit electric capability (MWe) and whether it produces electricity for sale (to confirm EGU status)
Annual and multi‑year heat input by fuel (MMBtu) to determine percent oil use and to compute liquid‑oil capacity factor
Maximum hourly heat input rating (to use in the capacity‑factor formula) and recent annual operating hours or heat input (low capacity factor claim)
Location (Connecticut — continental U.S.) and confirmation that the unit primarily burns No.2/No.4 fuel oil with only small natural gas use

candidates.name: Definitions (Subpart CC)

criteria.check: Determine whether the combustion unit fits the definition of 'flare' (a combustion device lacking an enclosed combustion chamber that uses an uncontrolled volume of ambient air to burn gases).
Determine whether the unit is a 'combustion device' or 'control device' as defined (e.g., incinerator, flare, process heater, boiler).
Determine whether the vapor routing constitutes a 'closed vent system' (piping/ductwork not open to the atmosphere) or instead is vented directly to a control device/atmosphere.

you_should_check: Is the vapor combustor physically an enclosed combustion chamber or is it open to ambient air?
Does the combustor rely on uncontrolled ambient air for combustion or on enclosed/forced air supply?
How is the truck loading rack vent routed (piping/ductwork) to the combustor?
How facility equipment is labeled/designed (incinerator/process heater/flare) in engineering drawings?

candidates.name: Miscellaneous process vent provisions

criteria.check: If the emission is a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent, determine whether the owner/operator is using a flare to reduce organic HAP emissions (in which case the flare must meet §63.670).
If not using a flare, determine whether the control device achieves 98 weight‑percent VOC/HAP reduction or 20 ppmv (dry, corrected to 3% O2).
Determine whether the vent qualifies as a 'maintenance vent' (used only for startup/shutdown/maintenance/inspection), which is subject to different provisions.

you_should_check: Is the truck-loading-rack vent designated a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent under your facility's applicability determination?
Is the combustor the continuous control for that vent stream (not just occasional/maintenance use)?
Does the combustor achieve the numeric performance (98% or 20 ppmv) if it is not a flare?
Is the venting activity routine operating emissions or episodic maintenance/startup/shutdown?

candidates.name: Monitoring provisions for miscellaneous process vents

criteria.check: If a Group 1 vent uses a combustion device to comply, identify the required monitoring based on device type: incinerator (temperature continuous recorder), flare (pilot flame detection or §63.670 compliance), or boiler/process heater (temperature/in‑flame requirements tied to heat input).
If the combustion device is an incinerator (non‑catalytic), check that a temperature monitor with continuous recorder is installed in the firebox or immediately downstream of the firebox.
If the device is a flare, determine whether pilot flame continuous detection is installed or whether the flare meets the requirements of §63.670 (as of Jan 30, 2019).

If using a boiler or process heater to comply, determine whether the vent stream is introduced into the flame zone and whether the unit's design heat input triggers monitoring exemptions or requirements.

you_should_check: Which device type best describes the vapor combustor (incinerator, flare, boiler/process heater)?
If incinerator or boiler/heater, where can a temperature sensor be installed to meet §63.644 placement requirements?
If claiming flare, is continuous pilot flame detection or full §63.670 compliance available?
What is the design heat input (MW) if combustor could be a boiler/process heater?

candidates.name: Requirements for flare control devices

criteria.check: If the control device is a flare used for an emission point subject to this subpart, the flare must meet the applicable requirements of §63.670 and §63.671 by the effective date specified.

If the device is a flare, determine whether a pilot flame is present at all times when regulated material is routed to the flare (each 15‑minute block with any minute without pilot while vented is a deviation).

For pressure‑assisted flares with burner stages that cross‑light, determine whether each stage has redundant pilots or complies with cross‑light performance demonstration and burner spacing requirements.

If the unit is a flare, determine whether you must calculate flare tip velocity (Vtip) and compare to operating limits using 15‑minute cumulative flow and tip area calculations (applies to tip velocity limits).

you_should_check: Can the combustor meet continuous pilot‑flame operation when truck‑rack vapors are routed to it?
Is the combustor a pressure‑assisted flare with staged burners (i.e., does cross‑lighting/spacing apply)?
Can you obtain continuous flow/area/temperature/pressure data needed to calculate Vtip if the device is a flare?
Are you prepared to meet the §63.670 recordkeeping/measurement requirements if it is a flare?

candidates.name: Requirements for flare monitoring systems

criteria.check: If a CPMS is installed to comply with §63.670, ensure the CPMS meets accuracy/calibration table requirements, completes one measurement cycle per 15‑minute period, and operates continuously when regulated emissions are routed to the flare.

Develop a CPMS monitoring plan that identifies the specific flare and flare type, the parameter(s) to be monitored and expected ranges, and describes monitoring equipment and probe locations/justification.

If a CPMS (except pilot flame monitors) goes out of control (calibration drift exceeds allowed limits), follow out‑of‑control corrective actions and exclude out‑of‑control data from 15‑minute averages.
Ensure CPMS data reduction rules are followed (rounding, exclusion of non‑operation periods, exclusion of out‑of‑control periods) for 15‑minute block averages.

you_should_check: Will you install CPMS for pilot flame, flow, NHV, or other parameters required by §63.670?
Can you document a CPMS monitoring plan with equipment, probe location, expected ranges, and QA/QC per §63.671(b)?
Can the CPMS be operated and recorded at least once per 15‑minute block while regulated vapors are routed to the unit?
Do you have procedures to identify and correct out‑of‑control CPMS periods and to exclude those data from averages?

candidates.name: Web coating lines (paper and other webs)

criteria.check: This subpart applies at each new and existing facility that is a major source of HAP at which web coating lines are operated.

A web coating line is present if one or more work stations applies a continuous layer of liquid or semi‑liquid coating material across the entire width or any portion of the width of a web substrate and has associated curing/drying equipment located between an unwind/feed station and a rewind/cutting station.
The substrate is a 'web' only if it is a continuous substrate (e.g., paper) that is flexible enough to be wound or unwound as rolls.
If web coating lines are present, the affected source is the collection of all web coating lines at the facility (subject to specific exclusions listed in §63.3300(a)–(g)).

you_should_check: Whether the mica paper line is fed from an unwind/roll and is a continuous, flexible substrate that is wound/unwound (i.e., meets the 'web' definition).
Whether the roll-fed line deposits a continuous liquid/semi-liquid coating across the web width and includes curing/drying equipment between feed and rewind.
Whether the sheet-handled line consists of discrete sheets (not wound/unwound rolls) and therefore does not meet the 'web' definition.
Whether the facility is a major source of HAP (per §63.2) so that subpart JJJJ would apply if web coating lines are present.

candidates.name: Natural Gas Transmission and Storage — Glycol Dehydration Units

criteria.check: Confirm the facility is a natural gas transmission and storage facility that is a major source of HAPs (Subpart applies only to such facilities).
Confirm the unit in question is an affected glycol dehydration unit (large or existing/new small unit as defined in this subpart).
Determine whether the reboiler vent is a 'glycol dehydration unit process vent' (definition explicitly includes the glycol dehydration unit reboiler vent).

If the unit is required to be controlled under §63.1275, determine whether the reboiler would be used as the required control device (large units must connect the process vent to a control device through a closed‑vent system, and if a boiler or process heater is used as the control device the vent stream must be introduced into the flame zone).

If the vent gas would be injected into the flame zone (i.e., reused as fuel), confirm how this subpart treats such reuse (the definition describes equipment types considered control devices and notes that routing/use/reuse into an enclosed combustion device has specific treatment).
Confirm whether a closed‑vent system connection is present or required (closed‑vent systems must route all gases from the emissions unit to the control device and have no detectable emissions).

you_should_check: Is the facility located and operated as a natural gas transmission and storage site and classified as a major HAP source?
Is the unit a glycol dehydration unit and is it designated large or small per the definitions?
Is the glycol reboiler vent considered the process vent and currently routed to atmosphere, a flare, or injected into a combustion device/flame zone?

Would the reboiler be serving as a control device (i.e., accept/process vent gas and have the vent stream introduced into its flame zone) and thus be treated under the control‑device provisions cited?

candidates.name: EAF steelmaking area source (Subpart YYYYY)

criteria.check: Whether you own or operate an electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking facility that is an area source of HAP emissions.
Whether your furnace meets the regulatory definition of an electric arc furnace (produces molten steel and heats the charge with electric arcs from carbon electrodes).
Whether the EAF is located at a steel foundry, because the definition of an EAF steelmaking facility excludes EAF steelmaking facilities at steel foundries.

you_should_check: Do you operate one or more EAFs that produce molten steel?
Is your facility an area source of HAPs?
Is the EAF physically part of a facility that meets the regulatory definition of an iron and steel foundry (i.e., pours molten metal into molds)?
Confirm the furnace design and operation meet the EAF definition (electric arcs from carbon electrodes).

candidates.name: Iron and steel foundry area source (Subpart ZZZZZ)

criteria.check: Whether you own or operate an iron and steel foundry that is an area source of HAP emissions.

Whether your facility meets the definition of an iron and steel foundry, i.e., melts scrap/ingot/other iron or steel and pours the resulting molten metal into molds to produce final or near‑final shape products.
For an existing affected source, whether your facility's annual metal melt production for calendar year 2008 was 20,000 tons or less (small) or greater than 20,000 tons (large).
For a new affected source, whether your facility's annual metal melt capacity at startup is 10,000 tons or less (small) or greater than 10,000 tons (large).

you_should_check: Do you pour molten metal into molds to make final or near‑final products, or do you use an alternative process (e.g., water atomization)?
What was your annual metal melt production in 2008 (if existing) or your annual metal melt capacity at startup (if new)?
Are you an area source (not a major source) of HAPs?
Confirm the facility is not solely R&D or producing noncommercial castings (per the foundry definition).

candidates.name: Iron and steel foundry (Subpart EEEEE)

criteria.check: Whether the affected source is each new or existing iron and steel foundry (i.e., whether your facility qualifies as an iron and steel foundry).

Whether your operations include the covered processes listed (metal melting furnaces, pouring areas/stations, automated cooling/shakeout lines, mold and core making lines, or fugitive emissions from foundry operations).
If existing, whether you commenced construction or reconstruction of the affected source before December 23, 2002 (existing vs new determination).
Whether the regulatory definition of iron and steel foundry applies to your facility (melting scrap/ingot and pouring molten metal into molds to produce castings).

you_should_check: Do you have pouring areas, mold/core making, or other foundry operations listed in 63.7682(b), or do you use water atomization instead of pouring?
Was construction/reconstruction of your facility before or after Dec 23, 2002?
Does your facility meet the 63.10906 foundry definition (particularly the requirement to pour molten metal into molds)?
Confirm which specific processes and emission points are present (metal melting furnaces, pouring stations, cooling/shotblasting lines, etc.).

candidates.name: Area‑source industrial/commercial/institutional boilers (Subpart JJJJJJ)

criteria.check: Determine whether you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler (as defined in §63.11237) that is located at, or is part of, an area source of HAP; if so, you meet the basic applicability trigger in §63.11193.

Determine whether each boiler meets the subpart’s gas‑fired boiler exemption (i.e., is a ‘gas‑fired boiler’ as defined in §63.11237); boilers that qualify as gas‑fired are not subject to this subpart per §63.11195(e).

Determine whether any boiler is an electric utility steam generating unit (EGU) as defined in §63.11237 (e.g., >25 MW and supplies electricity for sale); EGUs are not subject to this subpart per §63.11195(k).

If subject, determine whether the boiler effectively burns a single fuel type (i.e., uses a supplemental fuel only for startup, shutdown, or transient flame stability), because boilers that burn a single fuel are exempt from the fuel‑analysis requirement referenced in §63.11211(a).

you_should_check: Confirm the facility is an area source of HAP (not an area/source determination elsewhere).
Confirm each boiler’s category (industrial, commercial, or institutional) per the definitions in §63.11237.
Confirm whether each boiler is a ‘gas‑fired boiler’ per §63.11237 (fuel types allowed in permits, normal primary fuel) and whether on‑site fuel handling/equipment would indicate otherwise.

Confirm whether any unit meets the EGU definition in §63.11237 (nameplate capacity, percent of electricity sold), and confirm the purpose, frequency, and hours of permitted fuel oil firing (curtailment/tests vs. startup/shutdown/transient flame stability).

candidates.name: Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP) NESHAP

Whether the PCWP manufacturing facility is located at a major source of HAP (single HAP ≥10 tons/yr or combination ≥25 tons/yr).
Whether the affected source includes combustion unit exhaust streams that are routinely used to direct‑fire process units (for example, combustion exhaust that flows directly through dryers).
Whether the gasification/combustion units would be part of the affected source (new, reconstructed, or existing) at the PCWP manufacturing facility.

you_should_check: Does this facility manufacture plywood or composite wood products on site?
Is the facility a major source of HAP (confirm single and combined HAP potential/actual emissions)?
Does the gasifier/combustion exhaust routinely direct‑fire or flow through the PCWP dryers (i.e., is it integrated with the drying operations)?
Are the gasifier/combustion units located within the PCWP affected source boundary and under common control?

candidates.name: Boiler and Process Heater MACT

criteria.check: Whether you own or operate an industrial, commercial, or institutional boiler or process heater located at, or part of, a major source of HAP (subject to this subpart unless excluded by §63.7491).

Whether the boiler or process heater is part of an affected source that is subject to another subpart of this part (e.g., part of the PCWP affected source), which would make it not subject to this subpart.

If the unit is used as a control device to comply with another subpart (or part 60/61/65), whether at least 50 percent of the average annual heat input during any 3 consecutive calendar years is provided by regulated gas streams that are subject to another standard.
Whether any other specific exclusions in §63.7491 (a–n) apply to your boiler/process heater (e.g., types of units or uses listed there).

you_should_check: Is the gasifier/secondary combustion chamber defined/treated as a boiler or process heater at the site?
Is the unit located at or part of a major source of HAP?
Is the unit part of the PCWP affected source (subject to Subpart DDDD) or used to comply with another subpart/standard?
If used as a control device for another standard, did regulated gas streams subject to that other standard supply ≥50% of heat input over any 3 consecutive years?

candidates.name: Area Source Boilers NESHAP

criteria.check: Whether the boiler is specifically listed as, or included in the definition of, an affected source in another standard (if so, it is not subject to this subpart).

Whether the boiler is used as a control device to comply with another subpart (or part 60/61/65) and at least 50 percent of the average annual heat input during any 3 consecutive calendar years is provided by regulated gas streams that are subject to another standard.
Whether the unit is a gas‑fired boiler as defined in this subpart (such gas‑fired boilers are excluded).
Whether the boiler is covered by other exclusions listed (for example, hazardous waste boilers covered by subpart EEE), which would remove it from this subpart.

you_should_check: Is your unit listed or treated as an affected source in another NESHAP (e.g., Subpart DDDD)?
Is the unit operated primarily as a control device for another standard and do regulated gas streams to the unit supply ≥50% of heat input over any 3 consecutive years?
Is the unit gas‑fired according to subpart JJJJJJ definitions?
Is the boiler subject to any other exclusion in §63.11195 (e.g., hazardous waste boiler)?

candidates.name: Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP) NESHAP

criteria.check: Whether you own or operate a PCWP manufacturing facility (a facility that manufactures plywood and/or composite wood products, including facilities that manufacture dry veneer and lumber kilns located at any facility).
Whether the PCWP manufacturing facility is located at a major source of HAP (any single HAP ≥ 9.07 megagrams/10 tons per year or combined HAPs ≥ 22.68 megagrams/25 tons per year).

Whether the affected source would include your lumber kilns as part of the collection of dryers and drying operations and other process units associated with PCWP manufacturing (the affected source explicitly includes lumber kilns at PCWP facilities and at any other kind of facility).

If you are currently an area source that increases emissions or potential to emit such that it becomes a major source of HAP, whether you must be in compliance with this subpart by October 1, 2007 or upon initial startup of your affected source as a major source, whichever is later.

you_should_check: Do you manufacture plywood or composite wood products (or only lumber) at this site, or otherwise meet the PCWP facility description in 63.2231(a)?
Is your facility a major source for HAPs (is methanol or any single HAP ≥ 10 tpy, or total HAPs ≥ 25 tpy) based on potential to emit or actual emissions?
Are the lumber dry kilns at this site part of the PCWP affected source as defined (i.e., dryers/drying operations associated with manufacturing)?
If you become a major source, what is the effective date of that reclassification and has the compliance date for the subpart already passed?

candidates.name: General Provisions (Part 63) — applicability and affected source definition

criteria.check: Whether you are the owner or operator of a stationary source that emits or has the potential to emit any HAP and is subject to any standard, limitation, prohibition, or other federally enforceable requirement established pursuant to part 63.

Whether an area source that previously was a major source and becomes a major source again is subject to the applicable major source requirements established under this part immediately upon becoming a major source again, provided the compliance date for the major source requirements has passed.

Whether the equipment/operations (e.g., kilns, dryers) qualify as an 'affected source' under part 63 as the collection of equipment and activities within a single contiguous area and under common control that is included in a section 112(c) source category.

you_should_check: Does your facility emit or have the potential to emit HAPs such that it falls within part 63 applicability (per 63.1(b)(1))?

If reclassified to major by a permit revision, what is the effective date of that reclassification (i.e., when do you 'become' a major source) and have the compliance dates for applicable standards passed?
Is the set of equipment/operations at issue (kilns/dryers) contiguous and under common control such that they meet the 'affected source' definition in 63.2?

candidates.name: Chemical Manufacturing Area Source (CMPU)

criteria.check: Whether the CMPU is located at an area source of hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions.

Whether Table 1 HAP are present in the CMPU as feedstock, byproduct, generated in liquid streams, continuous or batch process vents, or produced as a product at concentrations above the thresholds listed in (a)(2)(i)–(iv).

Whether the equipment/operations at the facility meet the CMPU/affected source definition (NAICS 325 production, associated unit operations, storage tanks, transfer operations, surge control vessels, bottoms receivers).

Whether the area source installed a federally-enforceable control device on an affected CMPU that is necessary to maintain the source's emissions at area-source levels (which triggers a title V application deadline).

you_should_check: Confirm facility is an area source (not a major source) under §63.2.
Confirm which Table 1 HAP are present and their concentrations in feedstocks, byproducts, liquid streams, vents, or products relative to the concentration thresholds in 63.11494(a)(2)(i)–(iv).
Confirm that the processes and equipment meet the CMPU/affected source scope in 63.11494(b) (NAICS 325, associated tanks/transfers/etc.).
Confirm whether any federally-enforceable control device is installed and whether it is necessary to keep emissions below major-source thresholds as described in 63.11494(e).

candidates.name: Chemical Preparations Area Source

criteria.check: Whether you own or operate a chemical preparations facility as defined for this subpart.
Whether the chemical preparations facility is a stationary area source of HAP (area source as defined in §63.2).
Whether the facility has at least one chemical preparations operation in target HAP service (i.e., operations meeting the subpart's target-HAP-service definition).
Whether the chemical preparations operations at the facility are already subject to subpart VVVVVV (in which case subpart BBBBBBB does not apply to those operations).

you_should_check: Confirm the facility meets the chemical preparations facility definition in §63.11588 (identify operations that qualify).
Confirm area-source status under §63.2.
Confirm whether any operations are in target HAP service per the subpart's definitions.
Confirm whether those operations are already regulated under subpart VVVVVV (if yes, BBBBBBB is inapplicable per 63.11579(f)).

candidates.name: General Provisions — applicability and title V interaction

criteria.check: Whether you are the owner or operator of a stationary source that emits or has the potential to emit any HAP and is subject to a standard under part 63.

Whether the specific area-source standard (the relevant subpart) explicitly: (i) gives States the option to exclude area sources from title V, (ii) defers permitting, or (iii) fails to specify (in which case area sources subject to the standard are subject to the title V permitting requirement).

you_should_check: Confirm you are an owner/operator of a stationary source emitting or with potential to emit HAP and that a part 63 subpart applies to you.
Check the relevant subpart's (e.g., 63.11494) language on permitting to see if it: grants State option to exclude, defers permitting, or is silent (see 63.1(b)(2)(i)–(iii)).
If the relevant subpart is silent or directs title V applicability, confirm timing/deadlines in that subpart (e.g., 63.11494(e) deadlines).

candidates.name: Lead acid battery manufacturing (NESHAP)

criteria.check: Whether the plant is a lead acid battery manufacturing or component manufacturing plant that is an area source (if not, this subpart does not apply).

Whether the new Humidity Curing and Drying Oven Chambers are part of the affected source at the plant (the affected source includes 'any other lead-emitting operation associated with the lead acid battery manufacturing plant').
Whether the affected source (the plant) is classified as an existing or new affected source based on the applicable construction/reconstruction dates in those paragraphs.

For an existing affected source, whether a prior performance test using the same methods exists and either no process changes have occurred since that test or you can demonstrate the prior test (with or without adjustments) reliably demonstrates compliance for the new ovens.

you_should_check: Plant status/date of commencement (to determine existing vs. new per 63.11421).
Whether the new ovens emit lead and are physically part of the affected source.
Existence, date, methods, and results of prior performance tests for the existing ovens.
Whether process/equipment changes since the prior test could affect applicability of prior test results for the new ovens.

candidates.name: General provisions — performance testing (Subpart A)

criteria.check: Whether you are required to perform a performance test and, if so, that it must be conducted within 180 days of the applicable compliance date unless a waiver is obtained under this section.

If you plan to perform a performance test, you must notify the Administrator in writing at least 60 calendar days before the initially scheduled test date (allowing the Administrator to review/attend).

Whether you have prepared (and, if requested, will submit) a site-specific test plan including test program summary, schedule, data quality objectives, and QA program prior to conducting a required test.

Whether you can implement the required test method performance audit (blind audit samples) and include audit sample results with the performance test (or document commercial unavailability per the provision).

you_should_check: Whether you already have an approved waiver under 63.7 for the existing ovens and the scope/terms of that waiver.
Planned test schedule and ability to provide 60-day notice and a site-specific test plan if testing is performed.
Ability to obtain and use audit samples as required by the QA provisions of 63.7(c).
Whether you intend to rely on a waiver under 63.7 for the new ovens or to perform a new/combined performance test.

candidates.name: Extension of compliance and waivers/alternatives

criteria.check: Whether an extension may be justified because the source previously installed BACT or LAER for the same pollutant before promulgation (which can support an extension under the 'other reductions' provision).

Whether you will request an extension of compliance (including performance testing) in writing and meet any applicable submittal deadlines specified in those paragraphs (timing depends on circumstances described there).

Whether your written request includes the required contents: description of controls, a compliance schedule with milestones, interim control steps, and whether you are also requesting extension of performance testing.

Whether you understand the Administrator may grant an extension and that any granted extension will be written and specify the affected sources covered, termination date, dates for steps toward compliance, and whether performance testing requirements are included.

you_should_check: Whether the facility has previously obtained an extension/waiver and the terms of that document.
Whether the facility installed BACT or LAER (and dates) prior to promulgation to qualify under (a)(2)(ii) or (a)(5) if applicable.
Prepare the written request contents per 63.1112(a)(6) and confirm timing against the applicable compliance date.
Whether you are requesting that the Administrator extend or waive the performance testing requirement for the new ovens (explicitly state this in the request).

candidates.name: Stationary combustion turbines

criteria.check: Whether your turbine is a new or reconstructed lean premix gas‑fired stationary combustion turbine that must comply with the emission and operating limitations in Table 1 and Table 2.

Whether the turbine is not equipped with an oxidation catalyst, because if so you must petition the Administrator for operating limitations to monitor to demonstrate compliance with the formaldehyde emission limitation and you must measure these parameters during the initial performance test and continuously thereafter.

If you petition for additional operating limitations (e.g., %Load and inlet air temperature T1), whether your petition includes identification of the proposed parameters, a discussion of how changes in those parameters affect HAP emissions, how you will set the upper/lower limit values, the methods and instruments (and their accuracy/precision) you will use to measure and monitor them, and the frequency/methods for instrument recalibration.

Whether you can continuously monitor any parameters specified in an approved petition, because the subpart requires continuous monitoring of petition‑specified parameters to comply with the operating limitations in Table 2.

you_should_check: Confirm the unit is classified as a new or reconstructed lean premix gas‑fired stationary combustion turbine under this subpart.
Confirm the turbine is not equipped with an oxidation catalyst and that you intend to propose %Load and inlet air temperature (T1) as petitioned operating parameters.
Prepare the petition per 63.6120(f) documenting the relationship of %Load and T1 to formaldehyde emissions and proposed limit values.
Confirm you can measure %Load and T1 during the initial performance test and continuously thereafter, and that you have procedures for monitoring, accuracy, and recalibration as required.

candidates.name: Owners and operators of municipal solid waste landfills (NESHAP Subpart AAAA)

criteria.check: The collection and control system may be removed only if the landfill is a closed landfill and a closure report is submitted to the Administrator per the subpart.

The collection and control system must have been in operation a minimum of 15 years, or the owner/operator must demonstrate the system will be unable to operate for 15 years due to declining gas flow.

Following the procedures specified in the subpart, the calculated NMOC emission rate for the landfill must be less than 50 Mg/yr on three successive test dates that are each at least 90 days and no more than 180 days apart.

An equipment removal report must be submitted 30 days prior to removal/cessation that includes the closure report, documentation that the 15‑year control period has expired or that the system cannot operate 15 years due to declining gas flow, and dated copies of three successive NMOC emission rate reports.

you_should_check: Confirm the landfill's design capacity is ≥ 2.5 million Mg (to confirm Subpart AAAA applicability and NMOC requirements).
Confirm whether the landfill is legally closed per the subpart and whether a closure report has been or will be submitted (§63.1957(b)(1) / §63.1990 definition).

Confirm the gas collection/control system installation date(s) and whether it has operated ≥15 years, or assemble data to demonstrate it cannot operate for 15 years due to declining gas flows (§63.1957(b)(2)).

Confirm results and dates of three successive NMOC emission-rate calculations/tests (<50 Mg/yr), each 90–180 days apart, and that supporting sampling/calculation procedures follow the subpart (§63.1957(b)(3); §63.1959).

candidates.name: Plywood and Composite Wood Products (PCWP) NESHAP

criteria.check: Whether this subpart applies to your facility as an affected source at a PCWP manufacturing facility (applies to each new, reconstructed, or existing affected source).

Whether your reconstituted wood product press and reconstituted wood product board cooler are included in the definition of the affected source/process units subject to this subpart (presses and board coolers are listed in the affected source definition).

Whether each process unit (as listed in Tables 1A–1E and defined in §63.2292) will use a single compliance option because you must meet one compliance option per process unit and you cannot combine production‑based and add‑on control options for the same process unit.

For a reconstituted wood product press at a new or existing affected source or a reconstituted wood product board cooler at a new affected source, whether you will use a wood products enclosure or must measure and document the capture efficiency of the capture device (and submit that documentation with the Notification of Compliance Status).

you_should_check: Is your facility a PCWP manufacturing affected source (new/reconstructed/existing)?
Are the press and board cooler distinct process units as defined in §63.2292 and listed in Tables 1A–1E?
Which compliance option do you intend to use for each process unit: production‑based (Table 1A) or add‑on control (Table 1B)?
If using add‑on controls for the press or board cooler, can you meet the wood products enclosure or capture‑efficiency documentation requirements?

candidates.name: Rubber tire manufacturing

criteria.check: Determine whether you own or operate a rubber tire manufacturing facility that would be subject if located at, or part of, a major source of HAP emissions.
Determine whether your activities fall within the 'tire production' affected source (the rule explicitly includes 'tire repair operations' in the list of covered tire production processes).

Determine whether the materials/processes used in your retreading/repair operations are 'cements and solvents' as defined (the tire production affected source is the collection of processes that use or process cements and solvents).
Determine whether the facility is a major source by potential to emit ≥9.07 megagrams (10 tpy) of any single HAP or ≥22.68 megagrams (25 tpy) of combined HAP per year.

you_should_check: Whether your retreading/repair operations use or process cements and solvents (identify materials and usage rates).
Whether you perform puncture sealant application or tire cord production at the site (those are separate affected sources).
Your facility's actual and potential annual HAP emissions (single HAP and total HAP, in tpy).
Whether other stationary sources on contiguous property under common control should be aggregated when determining major source status.

candidates.name: Petroleum refinery catalytic cracking units (NESHAP)

criteria.check: Determine whether the source is a catalytic cracking unit subject to the metal HAP requirements in this subpart (i.e., whether the unit falls under §63.1564 and must meet the emission/operating limits therein).
Determine whether the catalytic cracking unit is subject to the NSPS for PM at 40 CFR 60.102, because units subject to that NSPS must meet the NSPS emission limitations described in §63.1564(a)(1).

If your regenerator does not introduce any other gas streams into the catalyst regeneration vent (complete combustion unit), you may use the alternative procedure in §63.1573(a)(1) by measuring/recording hourly volumetric air flow and gas temperature and calculating hourly actual exhaust gas flow using Equation 1 of §63.1573(a)(1)(iii).

Alternatively, if you have a gas analyzer installed in the regenerator exhaust vent prior to addition of air/other gas streams (measured upstream of a CO boiler), you may use the alternative in §63.1573(a)(2) by recording hourly air flow and continuous CO2/CO/O2 and calculating Qr using Equation 2 of §63.1573(a)(2)(iii).

If you elect Option 1b or Option 2 in §63.1564(a)(1), you may use the alternative procedures in §63.1573(a)(1) or (2), as applicable, to calculate Qr for the coke burn-off/PM emission rate equations in §63.1564(b)(4)(i).

you_should_check: Is the unit a catalytic cracking unit subject to Subpart UUU (§63.1564)?
Is the unit subject to the NSPS for PM at 40 CFR 60.102 (per §63.1564(a)(1))?
Does the regenerator vent introduce any other gas streams (if yes, §63.1573(a)(1) alternative is not available)?

candidates.name: Petroleum Refinery MACT (Subpart CC)

criteria.check: Is the plant site a major source as defined in section 112(a) of the Clean Air Act?
Does the refinery emit or have equipment containing or contacting one or more hazardous air pollutants listed in table 1 of this subpart (e.g., benzene)?
Is the wastewater stream an ‘emission point’/process wastewater stream as defined in this subpart?
Was the stream designated or changed from Group 2 to Group 1 as an addition or deliberate operational process change, and if so, which compliance-date/schedule provisions for Group 1 streams apply?

you_should_check: Confirm facility major-source status (CAA 112 definition).
Confirm the specific wastewater stream meets this subpart’s definition of a process wastewater/emission point and is designated Group 1.
Determine whether the Group 1 designation is treated as an added emission point or operational change (triggers §63.640(l) or (m) deadlines).
Decide whether you will use the compliance approach in §63.642(k) or the emissions-averaging approach in §63.642(l), as that affects which CC provisions apply.

candidates.name: Benzene Waste Operations NESHAP (subpart FF)

criteria.check: If the stream is a Group 1 wastewater stream, must the owner/operator comply with 40 CFR part 61, subpart FF (§§61.340–61.355) for that process wastewater stream?

Are periodic benzene concentration measurements, process or control-device parameter monitoring, and leak monitoring required and must operations remain within the permitted parameter limits consistent with subpart FF?
If subject to the wastewater provisions in §63.647, must the owner/operator comply with the recordkeeping and reporting provisions in §§61.356 and 61.357 of part 61, subpart FF?

you_should_check: Confirm that the stream will be designated and managed as a Group 1 wastewater stream under Subpart CC.
Confirm intent to control the stream under Part 61 Subpart FF and identify the specific monitoring/control methods to be used (e.g., closed vent and control, flare).
Confirm frequency and methods for benzene concentration monitoring and leak monitoring required by subpart FF and your plan for meeting those reporting/recordkeeping requirements.
Confirm whether you will rely on subpart FF control requirements in lieu of any Subpart CC-specific wastewater procedures where §63.647 directs compliance with subpart FF.
