candidates.name: Chemical Recovery Combustion Sources

criteria.check: Confirm the source is an existing kraft or soda pulp mill and the unit tested is a recovery furnace (as defined) that is subject to this subpart.
Confirm the compliance date for existing affected sources is March 13, 2004 (i.e., tests before this date occurred prior to the compliance deadline).

Confirm the performance test was conducted as a required initial/periodic performance test under this subpart, was based on representative normal operating conditions (not during startup/shutdown or malfunction), and that process information documenting normal operation was recorded.

If you plan to use the November 2003 test data to establish operating limits or demonstrate compliance, confirm the test data were obtained using the test methods/procedures required in this subpart and that you can certify no control techniques or processes were modified after that testing.

you_should_check: That the November 2003 particulate test was performed on the recovery furnace at your kraft/soda pulp mill.

That the November 2003 test used the subpart-required test methods/procedures (e.g., Method 5 or 29 or Method 17 with the required adjustment and sample time/volume/solvent requirements) and oxygen/flow measurement procedures.
That the November 2003 testing represented normal operating conditions (not startup/shutdown/malfunction) and you have records explaining and documenting those conditions.
That no modifications to the air pollution control device(s) or relevant control techniques/processes affecting PM emissions occurred after the November 2003 test and you can certify this.

candidates.name: Portland cement plants (NESHAP Subpart LLL)

criteria.check: Clinker cooler emissions (affected source) must not discharge gases exhibiting opacity in excess of 10 percent.

If subject to §63.1345 opacity limits, demonstrate compliance using the performance test procedures in §63.1349(b)(2) and use the maximum 6‑minute average opacity from the performance test to determine compliance.

If exhaust streams of a kiln with an inline raw mill and a clinker cooler are comingled, the commingled exhaust stream must be performance‑tested with the raw mill operating and with the raw mill not operating.

When clinker cooler exhaust is combined with kiln exhaust and sent to the same PM control device as a single stream, alternative (combined) PM limits and calculation procedures apply (i.e., combined‑source treatment must be evaluated).

you_should_check: Whether your facility is a major or area source subject to Subpart LLL (per 63.1345).
Whether the clinker cooler is an affected source and its exhaust is discharged to the common (commingled) stack with the kiln (63.1345; 63.1343(b)(2)).
Whether the kiln has an inline raw mill and confirm operating modes and the fraction/time the raw mill is on vs off (because commingled testing must be done raw‑mill on and off) (63.1349(b)(1)(vi)).
Whether the clinker cooler and kiln exhaust are routed to the same PM control device (i.e., controlled/combined) so the combined‑source PM provisions apply (63.1343(b)(2)).

candidates.name: General use coating subcategory

criteria.check: Confirm the operation is surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts or products as defined in this section (application of coating to a substrate, including associated surface preparation, cleaning, mixing, and storage).
Confirm the coating is applied by surface-coating methods (for example spray guns or dip tanks) and qualifies as a surface coating operation under this paragraph.

Confirm the coating does NOT meet the definition of high performance, magnet wire, rubber-to-metal, or extreme performance fluoropolymer coatings (if it does not meet any of those definitions, it is a general use coating).

Confirm the facility uses ≥946 liters (250 gal) per year of coatings that contain HAP and that the affected source is a major source (or located at/part of a major source), because Subpart MMMM applies only when those thresholds are met.

you_should_check: Is the material you apply characterized by the manufacturer/supplier as a rubber-to-metal coating or as some other coating class (get manufacturer formulation/use specifiers) (see 63.3881(a)(5) and 63.3981)?
How is the coating applied at your facility (spray, dip, other) and are associated prep/cleaning activities performed on-site (see 63.3881(a) and 63.3881(a)(1))?
Annual volume of HAP-containing coatings used at this coating operation and at the facility (liters/gal per year) (see 63.3881(b)).
Whether the facility is a major HAP source (potential to emit ≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP) (see 63.3881(b)).

candidates.name: Rubber-to-metal coatings subcategory

criteria.check: Confirm the operation is surface coating of miscellaneous metal parts or products (the subpart applies to surface coating of such parts/products).

Confirm the coating operation is performed using coatings that meet the definition of rubber-to-metal coatings in §63.3981 (operations are in the rubber-to-metal subcategory only if the coatings meet that definition).

If the material is used to bond two surfaces, determine whether it is an adhesive/adhesive coating as defined here and whether the material meets any rubber-to-metal coating definition/characteristics given by the supplier or in §63.3981.

Confirm the facility meets the Subpart MMMM applicability threshold (uses ≥946 liters/250 gal per year of HAP-containing coatings and is a major source or at a major source), because subcategory rules apply only within Subpart MMMM when thresholds are met.

you_should_check: Obtain manufacturer formulation and product classification to determine whether the coating matches the regulatory definition of rubber-to-metal coatings in §63.3981 (see 63.3881(a)(5) and 63.3981).
Document whether the coating’s primary purpose is bonding rubber to metal or some other protective/functional purpose (supplier use/intended application).

How the coating is applied and cured (spray/dip/heat cure) at your facility and whether the process description in supplier data aligns with the rubber-to-metal definition (see 63.3881(a)(1) and 63.3981).
Annual volume of HAP-containing coatings used and major-source status of the facility (see 63.3881(b)).

candidates.name: Wool fiberglass manufacturing NESHAP

criteria.check: Whether the product meets the definition of "building insulation": bonded wool fiberglass having a loss on ignition <8% and a density <32 kg/m3.
Whether the product is "bonded" wool fiberglass, i.e., wool fiberglass to which a phenol‑formaldehyde binder has been applied.

Whether the product is produced on (a) a rotary spin manufacturing line producing bonded wool fiberglass building insulation or (b) a flame attenuation manufacturing line producing a bonded product (rotary spin is defined in 63.1381 as any process other than flame attenuation used to produce building insulation).

Whether the wool fiberglass manufacturing facility is a major source (the subpart applies to facilities that are major sources or are located at a major source; the owner/operator may demonstrate non‑major status per 63.1380(c)).

you_should_check: Measure product LOI and density using the referenced test methods (see 63.1385(a)(7) for LOI and 63.1385(a)(9) for density and the applicable appendices).
Confirm the binder chemistry used (is a phenol‑formaldehyde binder applied?).
Confirm the manufacturing process for the line that makes this product (rotary spin versus flame attenuation) and that the line is producing the product as described.
Confirm facility major‑source status (permitting/annual HAP emissions) or whether you can demonstrate the facility is not a major source per 63.1380(c).

criteria.check: Determine whether the group of one or more polyether polyol manufacturing process units (PMPUs) and associated equipment is located at a plant site that is a major source (only PMPU groups at major sources are affected sources).
Determine whether the process unit’s primary product is a polyether polyol so the unit must be designated a PMPU.
Determine whether the PMPU uses or manufactures any organic hazardous air pollutants (organic HAP) during production (if it does not, most provisions of this subpart do not apply to that PMPU).
If the PMPU produces polyether polyols using tetrahydrofuran (THF), determine that the THF-specific process vent provisions in paragraph (f) apply (see linked monitoring/control cross-references).

you_should_check: Is the plant site a major source (potential to emit)?
Is the reactor/process unit’s primary product a polyether polyol (per the primary product rules)?
Does the PMPU use or manufacture any organic HAP during this polymerization step (including impurities vs intentional use)?
Is tetrahydrofuran (THF) used to make the polyether polyol in this unit?

candidates.name: HON process vent requirements (as referenced)

criteria.check: If the PMPU uses THF to produce polyether polyols, determine whether the process vents must comply with the HON process vent requirements referenced in paragraph (f) (i.e., §§63.113–63.118 as incorporated by this subpart).

you_should_check: Confirm whether THF is used in producing the polyether polyol in this unit.
Identify process vents associated with the unit that would be subject to HON-style process vent controls/monitoring if THF applies.

criteria.check: If a PMPU does not use or manufacture any organic HAP during production, determine that the PMPU is generally not subject to the provisions of this subpart and is not required to comply with the General Provisions (subpart A) for that PMPU.

you_should_check: Confirm whether any organic HAP are used or manufactured in the PMPU (if none, Subpart A general provisions are not required for that PMPU).

candidates.name: Paper and Other Web Coating

criteria.check: Determine whether your facility is a major source of HAP and operates web coating lines (this subpart applies to each new and existing major source at which web coating lines are operated).
Confirm whether your process meets the definition of a 'web coating line' (continuous application of a liquid or semi-liquid coating between an unwind/feed and a rewind/cutting station).
Confirm that the material you apply (glue/adhesive) is a 'coating material' as defined (coating materials include adhesives, including hot melt adhesives).

If the line coats more than one substrate type (paper and another substrate), determine the predominant activity (≥90 percent of mass of substrate coated during the compliance period) to see if this subpart or another applies.

you_should_check: Whether the facility-wide HAP emissions meet the major-source threshold (tons/year).
Whether the core-making step is a continuous adhesive coating operation between an unwind and a rewind/cutting station.
Whether the adhesive you use is considered a coating material and contains organic HAP.
Whether the line is excluded or governed by other subparts listed in 63.3300(a)–(g) (see candidate checks below).

candidates.name: Printing and Publishing Industry

criteria.check: Check whether the web coating line is stand-alone equipment that is part of subpart KK and is being included in the affected source under subpart KK.
Check whether the line is a product-and-packaging rotogravure or a wide-web flexographic press that is included under subpart KK.

you_should_check: Whether the equipment is classified as stand-alone printing/publishing equipment under subpart KK.
Whether the line contains rotogravure or wide‑web flexographic printing stations as defined for subpart KK.
Whether the owner/operator has included the line in an affected source under subpart KK.

candidates.name: Magnetic Tape Manufacturing Operations

criteria.check: Check whether the web coating line is subject to subpart EE (i.e., is part of magnetic tape manufacturing operations) which would make it not part of the affected source under this subpart.

you_should_check: Whether the substrate being coated is magnetic tape or the operation is part of magnetic tape manufacturing.

candidates.name: Surface Coating of Metal Coil

criteria.check: Check whether the web coating line is subject to subpart SSSS (surface coating of metal coil), which would exclude it from this subpart's affected source.

you_should_check: Whether the substrate being coated is metal coil (continuous metal strip ≥0.15 mm thick packaged in a roll or coil).

candidates.name: Printing, Coating, and Dyeing of Fabrics and Other Textiles

criteria.check: Check whether the web coating line is subject to subpart OOOO (coating/printing/dyeing fabrics and other textiles).
If the line coats both paper (or other web) and fabric/textile substrates, determine whether paper is the predominant activity (≥90 percent of mass coated) to decide which subpart applies.

you_should_check: Whether the substrate being coated is fabric or other textile.
If you coat multiple substrate types, the mass of each substrate coated over a representative period (at least one year or other reasonable period) to determine predominant activity.

candidates.name: Wood Furniture Manufacturing (Subpart JJ)

criteria.check: Whether the facility is engaged (in part or in whole) in the manufacture of wood furniture or wood furniture components and is located at a plant site that is a major source.

Whether the metal coating operations are coating metal components of wood furniture performed at the wood furniture manufacturing facility (metal components of wood furniture at a wood furniture facility are subject to subpart JJ).

Whether the metal coating operations are surface coating of metal parts/products other than metal components of wood furniture that meet the applicability criteria for the miscellaneous metal parts and products standard (subpart MMMM) and thus are excluded from subpart JJ.

Whether the plant qualifies as an area source under the volume or HAP emission limits and the 90% wood-furniture-emission criterion (250 gallons/month every month, 3,000 gallons/rolling 12 months, or ≤4.5 Mg single HAP and ≤11.4 Mg total HAP with ≥90% of plantwide emissions from wood furniture), because such area sources are not subject to other provisions of this subpart.

you_should_check: Confirm that the plant is a wood furniture manufacturing facility and its major-source status.
Determine whether each metal item you coat is a component of wood furniture (vs. non‑furniture equipment/parts).
Total gallons/month and rolling 12‑month gallons of all coatings/glues/cleaning/washoff materials used at the entire plant (to test the 250 gal/mo and 3,000 gal/12‑mo criteria).
If not components of wood furniture, whether those metal coatings meet the applicability criteria of other metal‑coating subparts (e.g., subpart MMMM) referenced in 63.800(d)(1).

candidates.name: Metal Furniture Surface Coating (Subpart RRRR)

criteria.check: Whether the items being coated are 'metal furniture' or components of furniture constructed entirely or partially from metal (see the subpart's metal furniture definition and examples).

Whether you own or operate an affected metal‑furniture surface‑coating source (new, reconstructed, or existing as defined in §63.4882) that is located at, part of, or itself a major source of HAP (subject to this subpart if so).

Whether the surface coating is of metal components of wood furniture conducted in an operation that is subject to the wood furniture NESHAP (subpart JJ), because such coating is excluded from subpart RRRR.

Whether the metal coating is performed as janitorial, building, or facility maintenance (routine repair/renovation of tools, equipment, machinery, or structures), since facility maintenance coatings are excluded from this subpart.

you_should_check: Identify whether the coated items are furniture or furniture components (match to the examples in 63.4881(a)(2)).
Confirm whether the metal coating operations are part of an affected source as defined in 63.4882(b) (coating operations, storage/mixing, pumps/piping, waste handling for metal furniture coating).
Confirm whether the coating work on metal equipment is routine facility maintenance/repair versus commercial coating of metal furniture/products.
If items are metal components of wood furniture, confirm whether those operations are subject to subpart JJ (which would exclude them from RRRR per 63.4881(c)(2)).

candidates.name: Web coating and printing (fabric and other textiles)

criteria.check: Does your operation perform coating or printing of fabric or other textiles (includes thread) as described in this subpart?

Does the shoelace tipping meet the regulatory definition of 'coating' (application of a semi‑liquid coating that, when dried/cured, forms a continuous solid film) or otherwise fall within the 'coating operation' definition?
Does the affected source include equipment used to apply the material and to dry or cure it (e.g., ovens, tenter frames, dryers) as part of the tipping line?
Is the affected source a major source (or located at/part of a major source of HAP) such that the subpart would apply to new, reconstructed, or existing affected sources?

you_should_check: Whether the tipping is applied to thread/cord (thread is included in 'fabric' per definitions).
Whether the methanol solution creates a continuous film when dried or is merely a small, localized treatment.
Whether any drying/curing equipment is used after application.
Whether the facility is a major source of hazardous air pollutants (HAP).

candidates.name: Slashing

criteria.check: Does your operation perform 'slashing' as defined (application of sizing compounds to warp yarn to bind/stiffen yarn prior to weaving)?
Does the tipping or other yarn treatment meet the regulatory definition of slashing or use slashing materials?
Does the affected source include slashing equipment used to apply and dry size on warp yarn?
Is the affected source a major source (or located at/part of a major source of HAP)?

you_should_check: Whether you perform slashing on warp yarn (vs. localized tip treatment of finished shoelaces).
Whether the methanol solution is a sizing compound used in slashing.
Whether drying equipment is part of the operation.
Major source status of the facility.

candidates.name: Dyeing and finishing

criteria.check: Does your operation perform dyeing or finishing of fabric or other textiles as defined in this subpart?
Does the tipping operation qualify as 'dyeing' (application of color in aqueous dye solutions) or 'finishing' (chemical treatment to impart properties) under the definitions?
Does the affected source include equipment used to apply, fix, rinse, or dry/ cure dyeing or finishing materials as part of the tipping process?
Is the affected source a major source (or located at/part of a major source of HAP)?

you_should_check: Whether the methanol solution is a dye or a finishing chemical (versus simple adhesive or treatment).
Whether the process includes fixation/rinsing or drying/curing steps typical of dyeing/finishing.
Whether the treatment is applied to the whole textile or only to small tip areas.
Facility major source status.

candidates.name: Applicability (Subpart T)

criteria.check: Determine whether the machine is a batch vapor, in-line vapor, in-line cold, or batch cold solvent cleaning machine that uses any listed halogenated HAP (methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, 1,1,1‑trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, or chloroform) at a total concentration greater than 5 percent by weight as a cleaning or drying agent.
Confirm the activity is not exempt wipe‑cleaning (e.g., rag or spray wipe), which is not covered by this subpart.

you_should_check: Identity and concentration (% by weight) of solvents used in the machine
Whether the unit is a batch vapor, in‑line (continuous) unit, batch cold (immersion) or in‑line cold unit
Whether cleaning is performed by wiping or by a solvent‑immersion/vapor process
Whether the unit is a continuous web cleaning machine

candidates.name: Batch vapor and in‑line cleaning machine standards

criteria.check: If the machine is a batch vapor or an in‑line solvent cleaning machine subject to this subpart, these design and operational requirements apply to existing and new units.
If the unit is a vapor cleaning machine, determine whether it has (or must have) a primary condenser (requirement for vapor machines).

If the unit is a batch vapor machine, determine the solvent/air interface area and whether it is ≤1.21 m2 or >1.21 m2 because that threshold dictates which control options or emission demonstration requirements apply.

If the unit is an in‑line cleaning machine, determine whether it is new or existing because the standard (control combinations or idling emission limit) differs for new versus existing in‑line machines.

you_should_check: Whether the machine operates with a solvent vapor zone (i.e., is a vapor cleaning machine) per the definition of solvent/air interface (63.461)
Measure or estimate the solvent/air interface area (m2)
Whether the machine is batch vs in‑line, and whether it is new or existing
Whether the unit has a primary condenser and other design features (covers, freeboard ratio, automated handling) referenced in 63.463(a)

candidates.name: Batch cold cleaning machine standards

criteria.check: If the machine is an immersion batch cold solvent cleaning machine, determine whether it is subject to the immersion‑machine requirements (tightly fitting cover plus either a ≥1.0 in water layer or a freeboard ratio ≥0.75).

If the machine is a remote‑reservoir batch cold cleaning machine, determine whether a tightly fitting cover over the solvent sump that is closed except during cleaning is employed, since that is the required design practice.

you_should_check: Whether parts are immersed in liquid solvent during cleaning (immersion batch cold) or solvent is applied from a remote reservoir
Whether the cold stage is heated non‑boiling solvent (falls under 'cold cleaning machine' definition)
Whether the machine has a tight cover and either a water layer or sufficient freeboard ratio (0.75) if immersion

candidates.name: Alternative standards (emissions‑based options)

criteria.check: If the cleaning machine has a solvent/air interface, you may elect the alternative standard that requires keeping a solvent addition/deletion log and ensuring emissions do not exceed the table 5 limits (kg/m2/month).

If the cleaning machine is a batch vapor machine and does not have a solvent/air interface, you may elect the alternative standard that requires logging solvent additions/deletions and meeting the cleaning‑capacity‑based emission limits in table 6 or equation 1 (use table 6 or eq.1 depending on cleaning capacity ≤ or > 2.95 m3).
If the unit is a continuous web cleaning machine, an alternative demonstration of overall cleaning system control efficiency ≥70% may be used in lieu of §63.463.

you_should_check: Whether the machine has a solvent/air interface (per 63.461) or is a batch vapor without an interface
The cleaning capacity (cubic meters) if there is no solvent/air interface to determine whether table 6 or equation 1 applies
Whether you intend to comply via the alternative emissions/logging approach instead of meeting §63.463 design/operational requirements
If continuous web, whether you will demonstrate ≥70% overall control efficiency

candidates.name: NESHAP for printing, coating, slashing, dyeing or finishing of fabric and other textiles

criteria.check: Whether the operation is a dyeing or finishing operation of fabric or other textiles (i.e., falls within the dyeing and finishing subcategory).

Whether the affected source includes the dyeing/finishing equipment and the solvent‑diluted materials are among the "dyeing and finishing materials" that are the regulated materials for the affected source.
Whether solvent that you add to a finishing (diluent) is part of the material "as‑applied" (the definition states as‑applied includes any added solvent).

Whether the organic HAP mass fraction for each dyeing/finishing material must be determined using the procedures and supplier/manufacturer information for the material in the condition it is received (prior to any onsite alteration) as required for compliance.

you_should_check: Is the stain‑repellent finish process you operate classified as a textile finishing (applied to impart stain‑resistant properties)?
Do you add (dilute with) solvent onsite or receive the finishing material pre‑diluted from the supplier?
Is the solvent actually applied to the textile as part of the finishing material (versus used only as a cleaning/maintenance solvent)?
Is your affected source a major source of HAPs (facility‑wide HAP emissions meet/exceed the major source threshold)?

Annual volume of coatings (including adhesives) used on the wood window components to see if it is ≥1,100 gal/yr

Which specific coating operations, storage/mixing vessels, and waste handling equipment at the plant serve the wood window coating activity

candidates.name: Aerospace manufacturing and rework NESHAP

criteria.check: Whether the facility engages in the manufacture or rework of aerospace vehicles or components and is a major source as defined in §63.2 (if both are true, Subpart GG can apply).

Whether the cleaning activities at the facility include hand‑wipe cleaning, spray gun cleaning, or flush cleaning, since each of those cleaning operation types is listed as an affected source under this subpart.

Whether specific cleaning tasks fall within the explicit exemptions: cleaning of electronic parts and assemblies containing electronic parts (63.744(e)(4)); and cleaning of aircraft fluid systems exposed to the fluid, including hydraulic fluid systems (63.744(e)(5)).

If a cleaning operation is not exempt, which compliance paths apply: (a) housekeeping/closed‑container requirements; (b) hand‑wipe solvent limits (meet Table 1 composition, or composite vapor pressure ≤45 mm Hg at 20 °C, or approved ≥60% volume reduction plan) per 63.744(b); (c) required spray‑gun cleaning techniques (enclosed system, nonatomized, disassembled‑in‑vat, or atomizing into a capture device) per 63.744(c); (d) flush cleaning into closed/enclosed collection systems per 63.744(d); and required solvent/usage/leak records per 63.752(b).

you_should_check: Whether your facility is a major source of HAP (to trigger applicability per 63.741(a)).
For each cleaning task, whether it is hand‑wipe, spray‑gun, or flush cleaning as defined in 63.742 and 63.741(c)(1).
Whether the specific tasks are covered by the exemptions in 63.744(e)(4) (electronic parts/assemblies) or 63.744(e)(5) (aircraft fluid systems/hydraulic fluid systems).

Cleaning solvent properties and formulations (HAP content, whether qualifies as non‑HAP material, composite vapor pressure, or meets Table 1 composition) and monthly/annual usage records needed to support the chosen compliance option per 63.744(b) and 63.752(b).

candidates.name: Miscellaneous Process Vents (Refineries)

criteria.check: Confirm the subpart applies at your plant site by determining whether the refinery is a major source and whether the equipment/vent emits or contacts one or more hazardous air pollutants listed in Table 1 of this subpart (i.e., applicability to petroleum refining process units).

Determine whether the orthoxylene rerun column vent is a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent (as referenced in §63.643) and whether that vent is a miscellaneous process vent/ emission point associated with a distillation unit (definitions in §63.641).

If the vent is a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent, the required control performance is to reduce organic HAP emissions by 98 weight-percent or to a concentration of 20 parts per million by volume, dry basis, corrected to 3 percent oxygen, whichever is less stringent, with compliance determined by measuring organic HAP or TOC as provided in this subpart.

If you propose to revise the monitoring plan (monitor parameters other than those specified), you must request approval (per §63.644(b)); monitoring equipment and monitored parameters depend on the type of control device used (incinerator, catalytic incinerator, flare, or boiler/process heater) as specified in §63.644(a)(1)–(4).

you_should_check: Confirm the refinery is a section 112 major source at the plant site.
Confirm orthoxylene (an xylene isomer) is a HAP present in the vent stream and that the vent is part of the petroleum refining/distillation unit.

Identify the control device type serving the rerun column vent (thermal or catalytic incinerator, flare, boiler/process heater, other) and, for boilers/process heaters, the design heat input capacity (≥ or < 44 MW).
Decide whether you will seek approval to monitor alternate parameters (i.e., prepare and submit the approval request required for alternative monitoring under §63.644(b)).

candidates.name: Hazardous Waste Combustors (Subpart EEE)

criteria.check: Determine whether your unit is a “hazardous waste incinerator” (the subpart’s defined hazardous waste incinerator includes the combustion chamber plus all associated firing systems and air pollution control devices) and whether it burns hazardous waste at any time.

Confirm whether you must (or have) conducted a comprehensive performance test, because operating parameter limits for the combustor (including firing system parameters) are established during the comprehensive performance test.

If operating parameter limits apply, determine whether you must use continuous monitoring systems (CMS) (e.g., thermocouples, pressure transducers, flow meters) to document compliance with those operating parameter limits.

For chlorine/HCl-related waivers: (a) whether you will petition to use CEMS for hydrogen chloride and chlorine gas in lieu of the corresponding operating parameter limits (petition option), per 63.1209(a)(5); and (b) whether you can perform the 1‑hour HCl‑equivalent emission rate calculation apportioning total chlorine to HCl and Cl2 using the historical highest Cl2/HCl ratio and most recent compliance-test gas flowrate (the criterion used to determine if an hourly rolling average feedrate limit on total chlorine/chloride may be waived), per 63.1215(b)(3) and 63.1215(b)(6)(ii)(A)-(C).

you_should_check: Whether the fluidized bed unit and its simple‑lance firing system are operated as a hazardous waste incinerator and whether hazardous waste is fed into it.
Whether an initial or subsequent comprehensive performance test has been performed and what operating parameter limits were established by that test.
Whether CMS/CEMS for the relevant parameters (pressure, viscosity surrogate, HCl/Cl2) are installed or feasible, or whether you plan to petition to use CEMS for HCl/Cl2 per 63.1209(a)(5).

Whether historical and most‑recent regulatory compliance test data exist (Cl2/HCl volumetric ratios, gas flowrate, and test results) to calculate the 1‑hour HCl‑equivalent emission rate per 63.1215(b)(3) and (b)(6)(ii).

candidates.name: Iron and Steel Foundries

criteria.check: Confirm whether your M-1 Pouring Area is part of an existing affected iron and steel foundry subject to Subpart EEEEE with the April 23, 2007 compliance date.
Determine whether the PM performance test was conducted within the timeframe required for initial compliance (no later than 180 calendar days after the compliance date specified in §63.7683).

Verify the performance test was conducted under conditions representative of normal operations (not during startup, shutdown, or malfunction) and that records document and justify that representativeness.
Verify the PM stack test used the specified Part 60, appendix A methods with sampling at the outlet of the control device (or source outlet) prior to any releases to the atmosphere.
Confirm the PM performance test included a minimum sample volume of 60 dscf per run and at least three valid test runs to comprise a performance test.
For the M-1 Pouring Area, determine whether the average PM concentration from the performance test met the Subpart EEEEE pouring-station/area PM limit (did not exceed 0.010 gr/dscf).

you_should_check: Exact date of the April 2005 PM stack test and whether the source was an existing affected source on that date
Complete test report showing methods used, sample locations, sample volumes, number of valid runs, and measured average PM concentration
Test-day process logs and production metrics (metal charged, pour rate, cycle types) and current production capability to assess whether test-day production rates represent current operations

Records of notifications: was a notification of intent to test submitted ≥60 days before the test and was the notification of compliance status (including test results) submitted within the required period after test completion

candidates.name: Mercury cell chlor‑alkali and mercury recovery units (Subpart IIIII)

criteria.check: If the unit is a mercury thermal recovery unit and you choose the continuous monitoring option, you must calculate the daily average mercury concentration for each operating day using Equation 2 (daily average).
If the unit is a mercury thermal recovery unit and you choose the periodic monitoring option, you must demonstrate continuous compliance using the procedures in § 63.8234(b).

If you choose the periodic monitoring option and your final control device is not a nonregenerable carbon adsorber, you must continuously collect data at least once every 15 minutes with a CPMS and record each 1‑hour average from all measured data values.

If you choose the continuous monitoring option, each mercury continuous emissions monitor must sample, analyze, and record the mercury concentration at least once every 15 minutes (enabling the daily‑average calculation).

you_should_check: Whether the affected vent is a mercury thermal recovery unit vent (i.e., your mercury recovery unit is covered as a ‘‘mercury thermal recovery unit’’).
Which monitoring option you will use: continuous monitoring (§63.8240(a)) or periodic monitoring (§63.8240(b)).
If periodic monitoring, whether your final control device is a nonregenerable carbon adsorber (different periodic requirements apply).
Whether your continuous monitor/CPMS can produce 15‑minute data and the required hourly/daily averages and meet any percent‑data‑capture requirements for the operating day.

candidates.name: Miscellaneous Organic Chemical Manufacturing (Subpart FFFF)

criteria.check: Determine whether the emission streams you intend to treat as part of the process meet the definition of a "batch process vent" in this subpart (only vents that meet that definition are subject to the batch-vent recordkeeping and reporting provisions).

If subject to this subpart, you must keep records that state whether each batch operated was considered a standard batch and estimate uncontrolled/controlled emissions for any batch considered nonstandard.

If you elect emissions averaging, you may estimate uncontrolled emissions for a standard batch using the referenced procedures and multiply emissions per batch by the number of batches per month when calculating monthly debits/credits for averaging.

You may submit a precompliance report to request approval for nonstandard operating/monitoring/recordkeeping approaches (including establishing alternative operating limits or providing data and rationale/engineering assessments to support alternative calculations or demonstrations).

you_should_check: Confirm which vents at the MCPU qualify as batch process vents under 63.2550.
Calculate uncontrolled organic HAP emissions per standard batch and the projected annual total (to see if thresholds/exceptions apply).
Decide whether you will elect emissions averaging so standard-batch multiplication per 63.2500(e) is used for monthly/annual estimates.

Prepare the precompliance submittal (engineering data, rationale, and proposed recordkeeping/operating limits) if you will request EPA approval for the alternative recordkeeping/definition of standard batches.

candidates.name: Pharmaceuticals NESHAP

criteria.check: Determine whether the material you produce is an "active ingredient" as defined (intended to furnish pharmacological activity or other direct effect; exclusions listed in the definition).

Determine whether your process operations include unit operations, storage tanks, wastewater streams, or waste management units as defined that would be part of a pharmaceutical production process subject to this subpart.

you_should_check: Is glucosamine hydrochloride produced at your facility intended/marketed as an "active ingredient" per 63.1251?
Do your reactors, product/process tanks, storage tanks, or wastewater units meet the definitions in 63.1251 and are they used in producing that active ingredient?
Is the facility a major source (potential/actual HAP thresholds) or otherwise within scope for NESHAP applicability (confirm with supporting subpart applicability rules outside the provided sections)

candidates.name: MON (Miscellaneous Organic NESHAP) Rule

criteria.check: Determine whether you own or operate miscellaneous organic chemical manufacturing process units (MCPU) located at or part of a major source of HAP (major source defined by CAA section 112(a)).
Determine whether the material(s) you produce are organic chemicals classified under 1987 SIC codes 282, 283, 284, 285, 286, 287, 289, or 386 (or excluded NAICS per paragraph (c)(5)).
Determine whether the MCPU processes, uses, or generates any of the organic HAP listed in CAA section 112(b) or hydrogen halide and halogen HAP (e.g., HCl).
Determine whether the process/unit is not already an affected source or part of an affected source under another subpart of part 63 (except the batch process vent exception noted).

you_should_check: Is your glucosamine HCl production organized as an MCPU (equipment set producing an organic chemical) per 63.2435(b)?
Does the product or intermediates fall into the listed SIC codes (identify the correct SIC/NAICS for glucosamine HCl production activity)?
Does the process use or generate organic HAP or hydrogen halide (confirm presence and identity, e.g., HCl) and quantify emissions to determine major source status?
Is the unit already regulated under another part 63 subpart that would preclude inclusion under FFFF?

candidates.name: HCl Production NESHAP

criteria.check: Determine whether you operate an HCl production facility that produces a liquid HCl product at a concentration of 30 weight percent or greater during normal operations.

Determine whether the HCl production facility (if any) includes the collection of unit operations and equipment from the point a gaseous HCl stream enters the HCl production unit through HCl storage tanks and transfer operations as defined.
Determine whether that HCl production facility is located at, or part of, a major source of HAP emissions (major source thresholds in paragraph (a)).
Determine whether the HCl production facility is also subject to subpart GGG (Pharmaceuticals), because if so subpart NNNNN would not apply per this paragraph).

you_should_check: Do you produce liquid HCl product >=30 wt% as an output of a dedicated HCl production unit, or do you only use HCl reagent/supply acid in your process?
If you do produce HCl, map the unit operations from HCl gas inlet to storage/transfer to confirm the facility boundary per 63.8985(a)(1).
Is the HCl production operation part of a major source (confirm single/combined HAP potential emissions)?
Is the HCl production function already covered by subpart GGG or another listed subpart (per 63.8985(b))?

candidates.name: Site Remediation MACT

criteria.check: Whether you conduct a “site remediation” at the facility (applicability starts with ownership/operation of a facility conducting site remediation, as defined in §63.7957).
Whether the contaminated soil meets the definition of “remediation material” (e.g., naturally occurring media such as soil that contains one or more HAP listed in Table 1 of this subpart).
Whether the site remediation is co-located at your facility with one or more other stationary sources that emit HAP and meet an affected-source definition under another 40 CFR part 63 subpart.
Whether your facility is a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥10 tons/yr of any single HAP or ≥25 tons/yr combined HAP).

you_should_check: Does the excavated soil contain one or more HAP from Table 1 and otherwise meet the §63.7957 remediation material description?
Is the excavation/temporary storage/backfill activity being performed as a site remediation project (confirm regulatory/remedial purpose and start/stop of remediation actions)?
Are there other on-site stationary sources that are regulated as affected sources under other Part 63 subparts (e.g., refinery units) located at the same contiguous facility?

Is the facility’s facility-wide HAP emission inventory above the major-source thresholds (and thus a major source), and alternatively, is the total HAP in all remediation material excavated at the facility <1 Mg/yr (to consider the recordkeeping-only exemption under 63.7881(c))?

candidates.name: Organic Liquid Distribution (OLD) - Subpart EEEE

criteria.check: Whether you own or operate an organic liquid distribution (OLD) operation that is located at, or is part of, a major source of HAP (if yes, the subpart may apply).

Whether the activities you perform (container-to-container and truck-to-container transfers) are part of an OLD operation—i.e., the combination of activities used to store or transfer organic liquids into, out of, or within the plant site.

Whether the liquids you handle meet the definition of 'organic liquid' (e.g., non‑crude/non‑condensate liquids containing ≥5% by weight of the organic HAP listed in Table 1 or crude/condensate downstream of first custody transfer).
Whether your operations include transfer racks at which organic liquids are loaded into or unloaded out of transport vehicles and/or containers (those racks are part of the affected source).

you_should_check: Is the refinery a major source of HAP (major source status)?
Are the specific transfers (container‑to‑container and truck‑to‑container) performed as part of the plant’s OLD operations (i.e., within the plant site and as storage/transfer activities)?
Do the liquids transferred meet the 'organic liquid' definition (HAP content, crude/condensate status, vapor pressure exclusions)?
Are transfers occurring at (or routed through) transfer racks as defined by the facility layout?

candidates.name: Subpart SS (storage/transfer rack emission‑limit requirements referenced by EEEE)

criteria.check: For any storage tank that meets the tank capacity and liquid vapor pressure criteria in Table 2 (or Table 2b as applicable), determine whether you must meet the emission limits in Table 2/2b and thereby comply with the applicable requirements specified in subpart SS.

If the collection of transfer racks at the facility meets the total actual annual facility‑level organic liquid loading volume criteria in Table 2 (items 7–10), determine whether each affected transfer rack arm must meet the Table 2 emission limits and thus comply with the applicable requirements in subpart SS.

you_should_check: Which storage tanks (if any) at the site meet the Table 2 or 2b capacity and vapor pressure criteria?
What is the facility’s total annual organic liquid loading volume to transfer racks (compare to Table 2 items 7–10 thresholds)?
Which specific tank(s) or rack arm(s) would be subject to Table 2/2b limits if thresholds are met?

candidates.name: Subpart WW (alternative control option for storage tanks referenced by EEEE)

criteria.check: For storage tanks that meet the Table 2/2b capacity and vapor pressure criteria, determine whether you will comply by meeting the requirements of 40 CFR part 63, subpart WW (control level 2) as allowed by this subpart.

you_should_check: Which storage tanks meet the Table 2/2b criteria and therefore are candidates for the subpart WW (control level 2) compliance option?
Do you intend to use subpart WW as the compliance route for those tanks?

candidates.name: Equipment leak controls (subparts TT, UU, or H referenced by EEEE)

criteria.check: Whether each pump, valve, and sampling connection that operates in organic liquids service for at least 300 hours per year must comply with paragraph (l) of EEEE and the applicable equipment‑leak requirements under subpart TT (control level 1), subpart UU (control level 2), or subpart H.

Whether a given pump/valve/sampling connector is 'in organic liquids service' (i.e., contains or contacts organic liquids having ≥5 percent by weight of the organic HAP listed in Table 1 to this subpart).

you_should_check: List pumps, valves, and sampling connections used in the specified transfers and confirm annual operating hours for each (identify those ≥300 hours/yr).
Confirm HAP content of liquids contacting each component to determine 'in organic liquids service' status (≥5% by weight).
If components meet the hours and service criteria, identify which equipment‑leak standard (TT, UU, or H) would be applicable.

candidates.name: Kraft/soda smelt dissolving tank (Subpart MM) monitoring

criteria.check: Whether you operate a kraft or soda smelt dissolving tank equipped with a wet scrubber (subject to the CPMS requirements in this section).
Whether the continuous pressure-drop monitoring device is certified by the manufacturer accurate to within ±2 inches of water gauge (±500 pascals).
Whether the smelt dissolving tank uses a dynamic scrubber that operates at ambient pressure (which would allow use of fan amperage or RPM as an alternative to pressure-drop measurement).

Whether minimum operating limits (including minimum scrubber pressure drop) were established based on values recorded during the initial or a previous performance test (set as the lowest 1‑hour average pressure drop associated with compliant test runs).

you_should_check: Is the unit a kraft/soda smelt dissolving tank covered by Subpart MM?
Do you have initial or prior certified performance test data (1‑hour averages) used to set the current pressure‑drop limit?
Does your installed CPMS meet the ±2 in. w.c. accuracy requirement, or is your scrubber an ambient‑pressure dynamic scrubber (so fan amperage/RPM could be used)?
Do you plan to rely on historical/performance‑test data versus conducting a new performance test to set a lower limit?

candidates.name: Wet scrubber operating limits (Subpart TTTTT)

criteria.check: Whether the wet scrubber is applied to meet any PM, PM10, chlorine, HCl, or dioxins/furans emission limit in Table 1 to this subpart, in which case you must maintain hourly average pressure drop and liquid flow at or above the minimum level established during the initial or subsequent performance test.
Whether you used the CPMS required in §63.9920 to measure and record pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate at least every 15 minutes during each run of the particulate matter performance test.

Whether the operating limits were established as the lowest average pressure drop and flow rate from any of the three compliant individual test runs (i.e., limits come from performance‑test run averages).
Whether you are subject to the continuous monitoring requirement to monitor hourly average pressure drop and liquid flow using a CPMS at all times.

you_should_check: Is your wet scrubber used to meet any Table 1 emission limits listed in Subpart TTTTT (PM, PM10, chlorine, HCl, or dioxins/furans)?
Do you have CPMS data (15‑min measurements) from the initial or subsequent PM performance tests (three runs) that established the current operating limits?
Have you sought to change operating limits without conducting a new performance test (note the procedures for revising limits require a performance test)?
Is the CPMS and the averaging (hourly/hourly average) being performed per the subpart's monitoring requirements?

candidates.name: Wet scrubber operating limits (Subpart RRRRR)

criteria.check: Whether the CPMS required in §63.9631(b) was used to measure and record pressure drop and scrubber water flow rate every 15 minutes during each run of the particulate matter performance test.

Whether operating limits were established as the lowest average pressure drop and lowest average scrubber water flow rate corresponding to any of the three individual test runs (i.e., limits derived from performance‑test run averages).
Whether any special exception applies (e.g., using historical certified performance‑test data to set a lower average pressure drop for a rod‑deck venturi scrubber on an indurating furnace).
Whether you propose to change operating limits without following the change procedures (notification and conducting a performance test) required to revise limits.

you_should_check: Is your wet scrubber subject to performance testing under the RRRRR subpart (i.e., to §63.9620 and operating limits in §63.9590(b)(1))?
Do you have the required CPMS 15‑minute performance‑test data (three runs) that established the current pressure‑drop limit?
Are you attempting to lower the pressure‑drop operating limit without submitting notification and conducting a new performance test?
Does any historical certified performance test exception apply to your scrubber type?

candidates.name: Steel pickling facility (continuous pickling lines)

criteria.check: Whether your facility operates one or more continuous steel pickling lines (i.e., qualifies as a steel pickling facility).

If a wet scrubber is used as the emission control device, whether systems are installed to measure and record scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if applicable, recirculation water flow rate, with those flow rates monitored continuously and recorded at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating.

Whether the scrubber minimum makeup and recirculation flow rates were established during a performance test in which each operating parameter was monitored continuously and recorded at least once every 15 minutes.

Whether the monitoring devices are manufacturer‑certified accurate to within 5 percent and calibrated at least annually, and whether records of scrubber makeup and recirculation flow rates and calibration/certification are being kept for 5 years with the most recent 2 years on site.

you_should_check: Do each of your two continuous pickling lines use wet scrubbers (and do those scrubbers recirculate)?
Date and results of the most recent performance test that established minimum flow rates and the recorded 15‑minute parameter logs from that test
Manufacturer calibration/certification statements and calibration schedule for each flow monitor
Location and retention (on‑site/off‑site) of scrubber flow rate records for the past 5 years

candidates.name: Hydrochloric acid regeneration plant

criteria.check: Whether your facility operates a hydrochloric acid regeneration plant (i.e., a plant configured to reconstitute fresh HCl from spent pickle liquor).

If a wet scrubber is used on the acid regeneration plant, whether systems are installed to measure and record scrubber makeup water flow rate and, if applicable, recirculation water flow rate, with those flow rates monitored continuously and recorded at least once per shift while the scrubber is operating.

Whether process offgas temperature is monitored continuously and recorded at least once every shift while in production mode, and whether parameters used to determine proportion of excess air are determined and recorded at least once every shift while in production mode.

Whether the plant established minimum process offgas temperature and maximum proportion of excess air during performance testing with continuously monitored parameters recorded at least once every 15 minutes, whether monitoring devices are certified to within 5 percent and calibrated at least annually, and whether records of offgas temperature and proportion‑of‑excess‑air are kept for 5 years.

you_should_check: Does the acid regeneration plant operate in hydrochloric acid production mode and use a wet scrubber?
Date and records of the performance test that established minimum offgas temperature and excess‑air values, including the 15‑minute monitoring logs
Manufacturer calibration/certification and calibration records for offgas and flow monitors
Where offgas temperature and proportion‑of‑excess‑air records for the last 5 years are stored and which 2 years are kept on site

candidates.name: Miscellaneous Coating Manufacturing (process vessels)

criteria.check: Confirm the equipment is located at or is part of a CAA section 112(a) major source of HAP emissions.
Confirm the equipment is used to manufacture coatings (as defined in §63.8105).
Confirm the equipment processes, uses, or produces hazardous air pollutants (HAP).
Confirm the equipment is not part of an affected source covered by another subpart of part 63.

you_should_check: Whether the 125‑gallon portable mixer functions as a ‘‘process vessel’’ included in miscellaneous coating manufacturing operations (see §63.7985(b)(1)).
Whether the mixer is located at/serves a major source and is used to manufacture coatings (mixing for coating production vs. other uses).
Whether HAPs are processed/used/produced in the mixer (types and quantities to determine ‘‘processes, uses, or produces HAP’’).

If you plan to consider alternative compliance, note capacity matters for emissions-averaging only: emissions averaging applies to stationary process vessels >=250 gallons at existing sources (see §63.8050(a)).

candidates.name: Site remediation NESHAP (Subpart GGGGG)

criteria.check: Determine whether you 'own or operate a facility at which you conduct a site remediation' (i.e., whether your company conducts the remediation at the facility).

Determine whether the material being cleaned meets the subpart's definition of 'remediation material' (material that contains one or more HAP listed in Table 1 and is the kinds of media/containers described).
Determine whether the site remediation is co‑located at your facility with one or more other stationary sources that emit HAP and meet an affected‑source definition in another Part 63 subpart.
Determine whether your facility is a major source of HAP (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP) for purposes of this subpart's applicability.

you_should_check: Who is the legal owner and who actually operates/performs the remediation work (does your company 'conduct' the remediation or does the other company retain operational control?).
Whether the materials excavated/treated are contaminated with HAPs listed in Table 1 of Subpart GGGGG (i.e., meet the remediation material definition).

Whether the remediation units are located on property considered your 'facility' (contiguous/common control per §63.7957) and are co‑located with other HAP‑emitting stationary sources at that facility.
Your facility HAP emissions inventory and PTE to confirm major source status (single and aggregate HAP tons/year).

candidates.name: Hazardous waste combustors (Subpart EEE)

criteria.check: Determine whether your units meet the Subpart EEE definition of a 'hazardous waste incinerator' (a device that is an incinerator under 40 CFR 260.10 and that burns hazardous waste at any time) and note that the definition states the incinerator includes all associated firing systems and combustion chamber equipment.

Determine whether each space you call a 'combustion chamber' is an 'area in which controlled flame combustion of hazardous waste occurs' (i.e., whether the rotary kiln and the secondary chamber each satisfy the combustion chamber definition).

If you have multiple firing systems or combustion chambers, determine the hazardous waste residence time for each, because the subpart defines hazardous waste residence time for multi‑firing systems as the longest residence time for any firing system in use at the time of waste cutoff.

For the dioxins/furans alternative emission limit that depends on temperature, determine whether the applicable temperature requirement is the combustion gas temperature 'at the inlet to the initial particulate matter control device' (≤400 °F average of test run averages) rather than a combustion-chamber minimum operating temperature.

you_should_check: Whether the rotary kiln and the secondary combustion chamber are physically and operationally separate areas of controlled flame combustion or are connected/treated as a single combustion zone
Whether the units burn hazardous waste (solid, liquid, gaseous) at any time and are subject to the incinerator definition in 40 CFR 260.10
Measured or estimated hazardous waste residence time for each firing system/chamber and which is the longest

Whether the temperature limit you seek to eliminate is specified in your operating limits as a combustion-chamber minimum or is tied to inlet-to-PM-control-device temperature (and what monitoring/PM inlet temperature data exist)

candidates.name: Surface Coating of Metal Furniture

criteria.check: Confirm your operations are surface coating of metal furniture (application of coatings to substrates) and that your cabinetry qualifies as metal furniture or components thereof under the definition in this paragraph.

Determine whether the affected source (see 63.4882(b)) at your facility is a major source (≥9.07 Mg/yr (10 tpy) of any single HAP or ≥22.68 Mg/yr (25 tpy) total HAP) or is located at/part of a major source.
If the affected source uses only coatings, thinners, and cleaning materials that contain no organic HAP, this subpart does not apply.

Verify that ‘contains no organic HAP’ is supported by determinations of mass fraction of organic HAP for each coating, thinner, and cleaning material using one of the methods/options in this section (e.g., Method 311, Method 24, supplier formulation data).

you_should_check: Whether the cabinetry and processes are within the ‘‘metal furniture’’ and ‘‘surface coating’’ scope of 63.4881(a).
Whether your facility’s affected source components meet the affected source definition in 63.4882(b) (coating operations, storage/mixing vessels, conveying equipment, and waste conveyance).
Your facility’s potential and actual annual HAP emissions (single-HAP and total HAP) compared to 10 tpy and 25 tpy thresholds in 63.4881(b).
Records or test/manufacturer data showing each coating, thinner, and cleaning material contains zero organic HAP per the determination procedures in 63.4941(a).

candidates.name: Secondary Lead Smelting

criteria.check: Do you own or operate any affected source at a secondary lead smelter (e.g., blast, reverberatory, rotary, or electric furnaces; refining kettles; agglomerating furnaces; dryers; process fugitive emissions sources; buildings containing lead-bearing materials; or fugitive dust sources)?

Does your facility meet the definition of a 'secondary lead smelter' and perform 'smelting' (chemical reduction of lead compounds to elemental lead or lead alloys in high‑temperature furnaces operated above 980 °C)?

Are lead emissions from process vents subject to the Subpart X concentration limits (existing sources: ≤1.0 mg lead/m3 per vent and flow‑weighted average ≤0.20 mg lead/m3; new sources (post‑May 19, 2011): ≤0.20 mg lead/m3 per vent)?

Can you demonstrate compliance by measuring vent concentrations and flow rates and calculating the flow‑weighted average (12‑month rolling average calculated monthly using most recent test data or CEMS data per Equation 1)?

you_should_check: Whether your CRT glass recycling involves smelting that reduces lead compounds to elemental lead/lead alloys at >980 °C.
Which equipment/processes at your site match the affected source list in 63.541(a) (furnaces, kettles, dryers, process vents, buildings with lead‑bearing materials, fugitive dust sources).
Measured lead concentrations and volumetric flow rates for each process vent (or CEMS data) to compute per‑vent and flow‑weighted average concentrations.
Whether your construction/reconstruction date makes you a 'new source' (subject to the 0.20 mg/m3 per‑vent limit) or an existing source.

candidates.name: Storage vessels with floating roofs (Subpart WW)

criteria.check: Is a record being kept of each storage vessel's dimensions, an analysis of its capacity, and identification of the liquid stored (records kept as long as the liquid is stored)?
Are inspection results recorded for each floating roof inspection, including vessel identification, inspection date, and, if failures occur, descriptions of failures, repairs and repair dates?
Are EFR (external floating roof) seal gap measurements recorded and do those records include the raw data obtained and any calculations performed?
Are records kept in a manner that they can be readily accessed within 24 hours and are they retained in hard copy or computer-readable form?

you_should_check: Which tanks are subject to Subpart WW (external floating roofs) at this facility
Whether you perform seal-gap measurements and inspections described in 63.1065(b)
Whether the retained records include the raw measurement data (field notes) and calculations
Whether records are stored in a form that is readily accessible within 24 hours (paper or electronic) and for the durations required

candidates.name: General provisions — recordkeeping (Subpart A)

criteria.check: Is the facility an affected source under Part 63 required to maintain files of all information required by this part in a form suitable and readily available for inspection and review, retained at least 5 years, with the most recent 2 years on site?
Are all required measurements needed to demonstrate compliance (including raw measurements) being maintained as part of the required records?
Are results of applicable performance tests, CMS performance evaluations, and similar measurements being kept?
Does the source meet the applicability criteria to be an 'affected source' under Part 63 (i.e., subject to these general recordkeeping requirements)?

you_should_check: Whether the plant/tanks are part of an affected source subject to Part 63
Whether inspection/measurement raw data are relied on to demonstrate compliance under Part 63
How long you currently retain field notes and electronic records and which 2 years of records are kept on site
Whether the raw field notes are considered required measurements or supporting documentation under your applicable subpart(s)

candidates.name: Organics emission standards for synthetic organic chemical manufacturing (Subpart DD)

criteria.check: Does the owner/operator of units subject to this subpart comply with the recordkeeping requirements in §63.10 that are applicable to this subpart?
Is a record kept for each inspection required by §63.695(b) that includes a tank identification and the date of inspection?
Are defects detected during inspections recorded with location, description, date of detection, and corrective actions (or delay reasons and expected completion dates)?

For external floating roofs, do records of each seal gap inspection include the date, the raw data obtained for the measurements, and the calculations of total gap surface area (and repair descriptions/dates if measurements do not conform)?

you_should_check: Whether any tanks are subject to Subpart DD at this facility (i.e., the source/category coverage)
Whether you perform inspections per §63.695(b) and seal-gap measurements subject to 63.696(d)(4)
Whether raw inspection/measurement data (field notes) are included in the retained records
Whether corrective actions and repair dates are recorded when defects are found

candidates.name: Storage vessel provisions (Subpart G)

criteria.check: If a vessel is Group 1 or Group 2, is a readily accessible record kept showing the vessel dimensions and an analysis of capacity (kept as long as the vessel retains Group 1 or 2 status and is in operation)?
If you elect to comply with §63.119(c), are records kept describing the results of each seal gap measurement including date, raw data obtained, and required calculations?
If you elect to comply with §63.119(e), are measured values of monitored parameters retained in a readily accessible location as specified?

you_should_check: Whether each storage vessel is classified as Group 1 or Group 2 under Subpart G
Which compliance option you have elected under §63.119 (if any: b, c, d, e, etc.)
Whether seal-gap measurements are being performed and whether raw data/calculations are kept
Whether vessel dimension/capacity records are kept while the vessel retains its Group status

candidates.name: National Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants for Area Sources (Subpart HHHHHHH)

criteria.check: Are records kept of storage vessel dimensions, an analysis of capacity, and identification of the liquid stored for each storage vessel covered by this subpart?
For internal and external floating roof storage vessels, are the records required in §63.1065 of subpart WW (including raw data for seal gap measurements) maintained?
Are copies of reports, notifications, and supporting documentation (and current site-specific plans) retained as required by this subpart?

you_should_check: Whether your facility/tanks are subject to Subpart HHHHHHH
Whether floating roof tanks at the site are covered and thus require maintaining §63.1065 records under 63.11990(b)(5)
Whether copies of notifications/reports and site-specific plans are being retained
Whether raw inspection/measurement data are stored together with electronic records

candidates.name: Area Source Standards for Plating and Polishing Operations

criteria.check: Whether your plant is a 'plating and polishing facility' engaged in one or more listed processes (non‑chromium electroplating; electroless plating; non‑electrolytic metal coating such as chromate conversion coating; dry mechanical polishing; electroforming; or electropolishing).
Whether the facility is an area source (potential to emit <10 tpy of any single HAP and <25 tpy combined HAP).
Whether the facility uses or has emissions of plating and polishing metal HAP (compounds or elemental forms of cadmium, chromium, lead, manganese, or nickel, per the subpart definition).
Whether the specific process unit(s) are subject to 40 CFR part 63 subpart N (chromium electroplating/anodizing), because process units subject to subpart N are excluded from this subpart.

you_should_check: Which listed plating/polishing process(es) your tanks actually perform (is it non‑chromium electroplating, electropolishing, electroless, chromate conversion, etc.).
Facility potential to emit (PTE) for individual and combined HAP to confirm area‑source status.
Whether the bath/tank contains plating/polishing metal HAP (e.g., chromium) as used.
Whether the tank/process meets the criteria for subpart N (see subpart N checks) so that subpart WWWWWW would be precluded.

candidates.name: National Emission Standards for Chromium Emissions from Hard and Decorative Chromium Electroplating and Chromium Anodizing Tanks

criteria.check: Whether the affected source is a chromium electroplating or chromium anodizing tank at a facility performing hard chromium electroplating, decorative chromium electroplating, or chromium anodizing (i.e., whether your tank is a chromium electroplating/anodizing tank).
Whether the process meets the definition of 'chromium anodizing' (an electrolytic process using a chromic acid solution in which the part to be anodized acts as the anode).

Whether the tank is actually a process tank in which neither chromium electroplating nor chromium anodizing is taking place (the section explicitly lists 'etching tanks' as an example of tanks not subject to this subpart).

Whether the tank has the typical components of a chromium anodizing tank (e.g., rectifiers/voltage control, circulation pumps, heat exchangers, air agitation systems) consistent with the subpart's tank definitions.

you_should_check: Whether the tank uses chromic acid and the part functions as the anode (matches the chromium anodizing definition).
Whether electrical/electrolytic current is applied in the tank (not a non‑electrolytic conversion or etching tank).
Whether the tank includes rectifiers/ancillary equipment typical of chromium anodizing/electroplating tanks.
Whether the tank/process might instead be an etching or non‑electrolytic tank (examples in 63.340(c)), which would indicate this subpart does not apply.

candidates.name: Area Sources: Carbon Black Production

criteria.check: Are you the owner or operator of a carbon black production facility that is an area source of HAP emissions?

Does each carbon-black recovery/heating process unit at your facility qualify as a 'carbon black production process unit' (the affected source includes each such unit and associated waste/wastewater/equipment)?
For each affected process unit, did construction or reconstruction commence on or before April 4, 2007 (existing) or after April 4, 2007 (new)?
Will you meet the requirements referenced in §63.1103(f) of subpart YY as required by this subpart?

you_should_check: Whether your shredded-tire heating/recovery operations are considered 'carbon black production' per the subpart's definitions
Whether the facility is classified as an area source of HAPs (not a major source)
Construction/reconstruction dates for each process unit to classify new vs existing
Whether you can comply with the §63.1103(f) requirements referenced in §63.11402

candidates.name: Source-category specific requirements (subpart YY)

Follow any applicability-assessment procedures/tables referenced in §63.1103 to determine applicable control requirements

you_should_check: Review §§63.1–63.5 and §§63.11–63.16 for general compliance, notification, monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting obligations that would apply if MMMMMM applies

Whether you elect to use the "emission rate with add-on controls" compliance option (i.e., include emission reductions from emission capture systems and add-on controls in a rolling 12‑month organic HAP emission rate).

Whether, to use that compliance option you can demonstrate initial compliance by meeting the applicable emission limits, operating limits, and work practice standards and by calculating organic HAP emission reduction using Equation 1 (apply capture efficiency and add‑on control DRE) and measuring/recording capture efficiency and DRE per the procedures referenced in §63.4561(h).

Whether the proposed add‑on control (the boiler) is a device other than those listed in Table 1 such that you must apply to the Administrator for approval of alternative monitoring under the provision cited in §63.4492(c).

you_should_check: That the two coating lines are for "plastic part and product" items (at least one piece formed from resin).
Monthly volumes and mass fraction of methanol (and other organic HAP) in coatings/thinners/cleaning materials to size emission rate calculations and Equation 1 inputs.

Whether emissions from the coating lines can be captured and routed to the boiler (capture system design and expected capture efficiency) and whether the boiler can achieve and be tested for a DRE appropriate for Equation 1.

Whether the boiler type is listed in Table 1 (or not); if not, be prepared to request Administrator approval for alternative monitoring and to perform required performance testing to establish operating limits.

candidates.name: Engine test cells and stands

criteria.check: Whether the apparatus in question is an engine test cell/stand (any apparatus used for testing uninstalled stationary or uninstalled mobile engines).
Whether the test cells/stands are located at a major source of HAP emissions (PTE ≥10 tpy for any single HAP or ≥25 tpy for combined HAP).

Whether the affected source is existing (construction/reconstruction commenced on or before May 14, 2002), new (construction commenced after May 14, 2002), or reconstructed (reconstruction commenced after May 14, 2002, per the reconstruction definition in §63.2).

Whether passive measurement and control instrumentation and electronics were part of the changes, because such instrumentation/electronics are not included in any affected source reconstruction evaluation.

you_should_check: Dates when construction/reconstruction activities commenced for the collection of equipment/activities that comprise your affected source.
Whether the site’s potential to emit meets the major source thresholds (single HAP ≥10 tpy or combined HAP ≥25 tpy).
Whether the items added/replaced are passive measurement/control instrumentation or other equipment.
Whether the changes occurred as a continuous program or under a contractual obligation (see §63.2 to determine 'commenced').

candidates.name: General Part 63 definitions (reconstruction/commenced/construction/costs)

criteria.check: Whether 'commenced' for construction or reconstruction was met (owner/operator undertook a continuous program of construction/reconstruction or entered into a contractual obligation to undertake and complete a continuous program).
Whether the work performed qualifies as 'construction' (on-site fabrication, erection, or installation of an affected source) rather than relocation or other excluded activity.
Whether costs of replacing minor ancillary equipment were included in your reconstruction cost calculation, because such costs must be considered when determining reconstruction.

you_should_check: Contracts, purchase orders, or schedules showing start/completion of work to determine when 'commenced' occurred.
Descriptions of the activities performed (fabrication/erection/installation vs. minor repairs/relocation).
Accounting of costs for replaced/added equipment and identification of any 'minor ancillary equipment' costs included.

candidates.name: Reconstruction cost exclusions (example for control equipment costs)

criteria.check: Whether, if reconstruction occurred, the affected source would be treated as a new affected source and subject to new-source requirements (reconstruction triggers new-source treatment).

Whether costs associated with purchase and installation of air pollution control equipment were included in the reconstruction cost determination, because those costs are not considered in determining reconstruction under this section.

Whether costs of retrofitting or replacement of equipment installed specifically to comply with the applicable subpart were included, because such retrofit/replacement costs are not considered reconstruction costs under this section.

you_should_check: Whether any purchase/installation costs you counted were for air pollution control equipment.
Whether any equipment replacements were installed specifically to comply with an applicable subpart and their costs were included in your reconstruction calculation.
Whether, if reconstruction is found, you have evaluated applicability of new-source requirements.

candidates.name: Asphalt processing (NESHAP LLLLL)

criteria.check: Determine whether the mist eliminator is a control device used to comply with the PM, THC, opacity, or visible emissions standards of this subpart, because if so you must conduct periodic performance tests and follow the procedures in §63.8687 and Table 4.

If you monitor pressure drop across the mist eliminator, you must meet the pressure measurement-device requirements (sensor location representative of pressure, minimum sensitivity, daily pressure-tap checks, quarterly accuracy checks, monthly leak checks, and periodic visible inspections).

If the mist eliminator is used to comply with the particulate matter standards, you may establish minimum and maximum pressure-drop operating limits using the manufacturer's specifications in lieu of the §63.8687 establishment procedures.

You must monitor and collect data at all times the affected source is operating (subject to the record-exclusion provisions for monitor malfunctions, repairs, and QA activities described in §63.8690(c)).

you_should_check: Whether the mist eliminator is the control device credited for meeting PM and/or opacity limits under Subpart LLLLL
Whether you plan to use pressure-drop as the parametric monitor vs. a COMS/CEMS or other CPMS
Location and model/specs of the pressure sensor (sensitivity >=0.12 kPa or transducer 5% of range) and the ability to perform the required daily/quarterly/monthly checks
Whether you intend to establish pressure-drop operating limits from the manufacturer's specifications and have the manufacturer's documented values and maintenance procedures available

candidates.name: Subpart A — Performance testing requirements (waiver/extension)

criteria.check: Whether the boilers are 'required to do performance testing by a relevant standard' (only then may a waiver under this section be sought).
Whether a waiver of performance testing has been or can be obtained under this section or whether alternative conditions referenced in this paragraph apply.

If asserting force majeure to delay or avoid a performance test, whether you can provide the required written notice, description of the event and rationale, actions to minimize delay, and proposed test date to the Administrator as soon as practicable.

you_should_check: Whether the applicable standard (e.g., Subpart JJJJJJ) actually requires the CO performance test for each boiler (see Subpart criteria).
Whether you intend to seek a formal waiver under §63.7 or instead to assert a force majeure (and whether notice can be provided before the test deadline).
Dates: the regulatory deadline for the next triennial test and whether you would notify EPA prior to that deadline.

candidates.name: Subpart JJJJJJ — Subsequent performance tests, stack test procedures, and general compliance

criteria.check: Whether each boiler has heat input capacity ≥10 million Btu/hr, because boilers ≥10 MMBtu/hr must conduct all applicable performance (stack) tests on a triennial basis per §63.11212.
Whether a continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) for CO is installed, because boilers that use a CEMS for CO are exempt from the initial CO performance testing in Table 4 to this subpart.

Whether the required performance tests must be conducted at representative operating load conditions while burning the fuel or fuel mixture that has the highest emissions potential for each regulated pollutant (which establishes how and when CO tests must be performed).

Whether an affected boiler has not operated on solid fossil fuel, biomass, or liquid fuel since the previous compliance demonstration and more than 3 years have passed, because in that case the subsequent compliance demonstration must be completed within 180 days after restart.

you_should_check: Heat input capacity (MMBtu/hr) for each of the 18 boilers.
Whether a CO CEMS is installed and operating on any boiler (and whether it meets applicable CMS requirements to qualify for exemption).
Date and results of each boiler's last CO performance test and the date the next triennial test would be due.

Planned cessation date for coal firing (April 30, 2020) relative to each boiler's scheduled triennial test date and whether any boiler will restart on solid fuel within 3 years of its last demonstration.
