candidates.name: Halogenated Solvent Cleaning (Subpart T)

criteria.check: Does any individual solvent cleaning machine at the facility use any listed halogenated HAP (methylene chloride, perchloroethylene, trichloroethylene, 1,1,1‑trichloroethane, carbon tetrachloride, chloroform) at a total concentration greater than 5 percent by weight as a cleaning or drying agent?

Does any unit on site meet the definitions of a 'solvent cleaning machine' or one of the covered machine types (batch vapor, batch cold, in‑line vapor, in‑line cold, continuous web) such that the machine would be subject to this subpart if it used regulated solvents?

If solvent cleaning machines are present, is the facility an 'affected facility' (e.g., a major source with solvent cleaning machines subject to the facility‑wide limits, or an area source with machines subject to the facility‑wide limits) so that the facility‑wide standards of §63.471 would apply?

If you operate solvent cleaning machines subject to this subpart, do you have a current annual reporting obligation (annual report by Feb 1 for machines complying with §63.463 per §63.468(f); annual solvent emission report per §63.468(g); exceedance reporting per §63.468(h); facility annual solvent emission report per §63.471(h))?

you_should_check: Whether any machines remain installed and whether they currently contain or are ever charged with any of the listed halogenated HAPs (identify solvents and verify concentrations by MSDS, test method 18, or engineering calc).
Whether machines were permanently removed or merely converted/idle (presence of a machine that could again be charged with regulated solvent can trigger applicability).
Facility status as a major or area source and whether any remaining machines would be 'affected facility' units under §63.471(a).

History of notifications/reports already submitted (initial notification, initial statement of compliance, last annual report) and whether any 12‑month rolling emission logs or solvent addition/deletion logs are being maintained per §63.471(b)(1) and §63.467/(63.471)

candidates.name: Organic Liquids Distribution (Non‑Gasoline)

criteria.check: Whether the affected source is the collection of activities/equipment used to distribute organic liquids at a facility that is a major source of HAP (i.e., is your plant a major source and are these activities part of the distribution collection).

Whether the equipment in question are transfer racks at which organic liquids are loaded into or unloaded out of transport vehicles and/or containers (i.e., do the racks unload hexane from transport vehicles).
Whether the transport vehicles are loading or unloading organic liquids at the transfer racks (transport vehicles are included while loading/unloading at subject racks).

Whether the storage tanks, transfer racks, transport vehicles, containers, or equipment leak components are part of an affected source already covered by another 40 CFR part 63 NESHAP (if so, they are excluded from subpart EEEE).

you_should_check: Is the plant a major source of HAP (≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP)?
Do the racks unload hexane from transport vehicles (i.e., meet the transfer rack definition in 63.2338(b)(2))?
Are the racks/tanks/vehicles assigned to or listed under another NESHAP (for example, as part of the vegetable oil production affected source under subpart GGGG)?
Are the unloading operations part of the facility’s organic liquids distribution operations (OLD) rather than exclusively part of the solvent recovery/production process?

candidates.name: Solvent Extraction for Vegetable Oil Production

criteria.check: Whether you own or operate a vegetable oil production process that is a major source of HAP emissions or is collocated at a plant site with other sources that are individually or collectively a major source of HAP.
Whether your vegetable oil production process processes any of the listed oilseeds (corn germ, cottonseed, flax, peanut, rapeseed, safflower, soybean, sunflower).

Whether the operations/equipment constitute a 'vegetable oil production process' as defined (continuous solvent‑extraction process that produces crude vegetable oil and meal by direct contact with an organic solvent such as hexane, including solvent storage/working tanks and solvent recovery system).

If the source meets the applicability criteria in §63.2832, whether it must comply with the subpart's emission requirements (i.e., you must follow the compliance options and emission limits in §63.2840).

you_should_check: Does your facility process listed oilseeds via solvent extraction (hexane contact) as part of a continuous vegetable oil production process?
Is the vegetable oil production process at your site a major source of HAP (≥10 tpy single or ≥25 tpy combined) or collocated with other major source operations?

Are the hexane storage tanks, solvent recovery equipment, and the unloading racks/transport vehicles directly part of the defined vegetable oil production process (e.g., feed solvent into storage/working tanks or solvent recovery system)?
Is the solvent used (hexane) received and unloaded directly into equipment/tanks that are part of the process components listed in §63.2872?

candidates.name: National Emission Standards for Pulp and Paper (Subpart S)

criteria.check: Determine whether your mill is subject to the Subpart S standards listed in §63.453(a) (i.e., the provisions referenced in §§63.443–63.450).
If subject, verify that each enclosure opening's closure mechanism is currently required to be visually inspected at least once every 30 days to ensure closure and seal.
If subject, verify that each closed-vent system is currently required to be visually inspected every 30 days for visible evidence of defects (ductwork, piping, enclosures, connections).

If you operate pulping-process condensate closed collection systems, confirm those systems are required to be visually inspected every 30 days and to comply with the referenced closed-collection monitoring/inspection provisions.

Any change to monitoring parameters, monitoring frequency, or averaging time requires providing the Administrator with the rationale, data, and calculations supporting the selected monitoring frequency for approval.

you_should_check: Whether this facility is regulated under Subpart S (which specific §§ 63.443–63.450 provisions apply).
Which closed-vent/enclosure or pulping-process condensate closed collection systems exist at the mill.
Current inspection procedure(s) and whether they are documented as “every 30 days.”
Data/engineering basis you can supply to the Administrator to justify a different monitoring frequency.

candidates.name: Closed‑vent systems and control devices (Subpart H)

criteria.check: If your closed-vent system is subject to Subpart H and is constructed of hard-piping, inspections are required as an initial inspection and then annual visual inspections for visible/audible/olfactory indications of leaks.

If your closed-vent system is constructed of ductwork, confirm it requires an initial inspection and then annual inspections according to the procedures in §63.172(g) (inspection procedures referenced in §63.180(b)).

If your closed-vent system contains bypass lines secured with a car-seal or lock-and-key, a visual inspection of the seal/closure mechanism is required at least once every month to ensure non-diversion.

If leaks are indicated by an instrument reading >500 ppm above background or visual inspection, repairs must be initiated within 5 calendar days and completed within 15 calendar days (unless delays allowed under §63.172(i)).

you_should_check: Whether this facility or specific closed-vent systems are regulated under Subpart H (i.e., applicable source definitions).
Construction type of the closed-vent systems (hard-piping vs. ductwork).
Whether bypass lines exist and are secured by seals/locks.
Current repair/response timelines and leak detection procedures.

candidates.name: General monitoring provisions (Subpart A, §63.8)

criteria.check: The Administrator may specify or approve minor changes in methodology for specified monitoring requirements and procedures (i.e., minor monitoring changes may be approved).
The Administrator may approve the use of an intermediate or major change or an alternative to any monitoring requirements or procedures; such approval is required before the alternative is used.

All continuous monitoring systems required under relevant standards are subject to the provisions of §63.8 (so Subpart A procedures apply to CMS/monitoring alternatives when the relevant standard requires CMS).

CMS must be installed, operational, and data verified as specified in the relevant standard prior to or in conjunction with performance tests, so any approved alternative monitoring plan must still meet installation/verification expectations.

you_should_check: Whether the monitoring you propose involves CMS or inspection frequency only and whether it qualifies as a minor vs intermediate/major change.
Prepare to request Administrator approval per §63.8 procedures and document the proposed change and justification.
Whether the relevant subpart explicitly refers monitoring to the provisions of §63.8 (i.e., your affected standard invokes Subpart A).

candidates.name: Continuous compliance monitoring timing rules (Subpart UUUU)

criteria.check: All time-period terms (e.g., monthly) in this subpart refer to standard calendar periods; you may change time periods specified in the subpart by mutual agreement with the Administrator as specified in Subpart A.
You may change time periods for completing required tasks by mutual agreement with the Administrator (the revised period remains in effect until changed).

When a provision requires completing a task during each of multiple successive periods, you may perform the required task at any time during the specified period provided it is at a reasonable interval after the previous period's task.

Except for malfunctions/quality-assurance activities, monitoring must be continuous (or at all required intervals) at all times the affected source is operating, including startup/shutdown/malfunction.

candidates.name: Polymers and Resins (TPPU)

criteria.check: Determine whether your plant/site is a major source and the containers are part of one or more thermoplastic product process units (TPPUs) that constitute an affected source.
Determine whether the portable containers managing waste/wastewater are considered 'waste management units' included within the affected source boundaries.

Determine whether the portable containers and their pressure relief devices meet the subpart's definition of 'equipment' or 'pressure relief device' (i.e., pressure relief devices in organic HAP service).

If the containers/pressure relief devices are in organic HAP service, identify that subpart JJJ imposes the pressure relief device operating, post‑release, and pressure‑release‑management requirements referenced in this paragraph.

you_should_check: Is the plant site a major source (per your Title V/permit/major-source determination)?
Are the portable containers part of a TPPU or otherwise managed as 'waste management units' associated with the TPPU?
Are the containers operated in organic HAP service (i.e., contain organic HAP) and for how many hours per year?
Are the pressure relief devices on those containers specifically in organic HAP gas/vapor or light liquid service?

candidates.name: Equipment Leaks — Pressure Relief Devices

criteria.check: Confirm Subpart H applies to equipment that is intended to operate in organic HAP service 300 hours or more per calendar year within a source that is subject to a specific subpart referencing subpart H.

If a pressure relief device is in gas/vapor (organic HAP) service, the device must be operated except during releases with an instrument reading <500 ppm above background (per the cited monitoring method).

After each pressure release, the device must be returned to <500 ppm above background as soon as practicable and monitored no later than 5 calendar days after the release to confirm the <500 ppm condition.

Determine whether the pressure relief device is routed to a process/control/fuel gas/drain (which can exempt monitoring) or whether it includes/consists of a rupture disk (which has different post‑release actions such as installing a replacement disk within 5 days).

you_should_check: Are the portable containers' PRDs intended to operate in organic HAP service ≥300 hours/year?
Are the PRDs in gas/vapor vs. light liquid vs. heavy liquid service (affects which requirements apply)?
Are PRD discharges routed to a closed vent system, control device, process, fuel gas system, or drain?
Do the PRDs include or consist solely of rupture disks (and if so, how are they operated/maintained)?

candidates.name: Pulp and Paper NESHAP (Subpart S)

criteria.check: Determine whether your pulping/bleaching/treatment units are subject to the standards listed (§§ 63.443, 63.444, 63.445, 63.446, 63.447, or § 63.450) because if so you must install, calibrate, operate, and maintain a continuous monitoring system (CMS).

If your bleach plant is complying with § 63.445(c) (bleaching-system outlet concentration requirement) then you must operate a CMS measuring gas-scrubber effluent pH or ORP, gas-scrubber vent gas inlet flow rate, and gas-scrubber liquid influent flow rate.

If you use a steam stripper to comply with the treatment requirements in § 63.446(e)(3)–(5) you must monitor process wastewater feed rate, steam feed rate, and column feed temperature (or, as an option, monitor methanol outlet concentration).

If you are proposing an alternative monitoring parameter or control-device parameter, you must install a CMS and establish parameter(s) and values following the § 63.453(m)/(n) procedures (including providing rationale to the Administrator) and support them with the initial performance test required by § 63.457(a).

you_should_check: Which specific pulping/bleaching/treatment emission units at your Mississippi softwood kraft mill are listed in §§ 63.443–63.447 or § 63.450.
Whether your bleach plant uses a gas scrubber subject to § 63.445(c) and can supply continuous pH/ORP and flow monitoring.
Whether you use a steam stripper for HAP treatment subject to § 63.446(e) and whether you will monitor the specified feed/steam/temp parameters or methanol outlet concentration.
Whether you will rely on an alternative monitoring parameter and be prepared to perform the initial performance test and submit the rationale/data per § 63.453(n) for Administrator approval.

candidates.name: Kraft/Soda Recovery Furnaces & Lime Kilns (Subpart MM)

criteria.check: If you operate an affected kraft or soda recovery furnace or lime kiln equipped with an ESP, you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS) meeting PS‑1 and §§ 63.6(h) and 63.8 requirements.

If your recovery furnace or smelt-dissolving tank is controlled by a wet scrubber you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a CPMS that records scrubber pressure drop and scrubbing liquid flow rate at least once every 15 minutes, using devices meeting the specified accuracy requirements.

If your semichemical combustion unit (or applicable unit) is controlled by an RTO, you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a CPMS that measures and records the RTO operating temperature at least once every 15 minutes with the stated accuracy.

If you seek to monitor alternative control‑device parameters (or use an alternative monitoring method) you must obtain prior written Administrator approval by submitting an alternative monitoring request with control description, test results, proposed parameters/operating limits, and QA/performance specifications, and establish operating limits during performance testing as specified.

you_should_check: Whether you operate a kraft recovery furnace, lime kiln, smelt dissolving tank, or other affected unit at the site.
Which air pollution control device(s) are installed on those units (ESP, wet scrubber, RTO, fabric filter, or other) and the device-specific monitoring requirements that follow.
If using a wet scrubber or COMS, whether your monitoring devices can meet the accuracy and recording frequency specs in § 63.864(e)(10) and (d).

If proposing alternative monitoring for recovery‑furnace controls, prepare the alternative monitoring request with test data, operating-limit development during performance tests, and the QA/performance specs required for Administrator approval.

candidates.name: Lime Manufacturing Plants (NESHAP Subpart AAAAA)

criteria.check: Determine whether your kiln(s) are a new or existing affected source and which compliance date in §63.7083 applies to you (new-source vs existing-source deadlines).
Confirm whether a continuous opacity monitoring system (COMS) must be installed at the outlet of your control device and must meet PS‑1/part 60 requirements.

If you have existing lime kilns, check whether you qualify to use periodic visible emissions (VE) checks (Method 9 or Method 22-style checks) in lieu of installing a COMS under the conditions in §63.7121(f)(1)–(3).

Verify that your written operations, maintenance, and monitoring (OM&M) plan has the monitoring procedures and installation/operation requirements for COMS/monitoring devices and has been submitted to the permitting authority as required.

you_should_check: Are the kiln(s) at your facility identified as affected sources under Subpart AAAAA?
Date of initial startup or date construction/reconstruction (to determine new vs existing and the applicable compliance date).
Whether the kiln(s) exhaust through a control device and the physical location where a COMS would be mounted (outlet vs other).
Whether you already have an approved OM&M plan and the permitting authority's stance on COMS installation deadlines

candidates.name: General Provisions (NESHAP Subpart A, §63.6)

criteria.check: Check whether the Administrator (or a State with an approved permit program) has granted an extension of compliance for your source consistent with paragraph (i) of §63.6.
Confirm the compliance date applicable to existing sources as established in the applicable subpart and whether the Administrator set or can set a different compliance date for existing sources.

you_should_check: Whether you have a written request or an existing granted extension from the Administrator or State permitting authority (and the documentation/terms of that extension).
Whether the subpart’s compliance date for your affected-source category is already specified or whether you must meet the default 3‑year maximum for existing-source compliance dates

candidates.name: Phosphate fertilizer production (Subpart BB)

criteria.check: Determine whether each of your three granular ammonium phosphate trains is a 'phosphate fertilizer process line' subject to Subpart BB (and which emission-limit table and compliance date in §63.622 applies).

Verify that for each process line you have the required continuous monitoring system (CMS) installed, calibrated, maintained and operated per your site-specific monitoring plan, and that it determines and permanently records the mass flow of phosphorus-bearing feed (equivalent P2O5).

Confirm your site-specific monitoring plan includes the schedule for conducting initial and subsequent performance evaluations, and check whether that schedule (as written or proposed) allows performance evaluations to occur within a five-day window prior to performance tests.

If you use a CMS, confirm that CMS performance evaluations are conducted 'in accordance with your site-specific monitoring plan' (and with the performance-evaluation provisions referenced in this section), so any alternative timing must be reflected in and consistent with that plan.

you_should_check: Confirm the three trains are subject to Subpart BB and whether they are existing or new units (to identify the applicable compliance dates in §63.622).
Confirm which control devices are used on each train (e.g., absorbers/scrubbers or fabric filters) since monitoring/CPMS and performance-evaluation requirements depend on the control device type.

Confirm you have a current site-specific monitoring plan per §63.628(c) on site (or submitted/approved), and whether it already specifies performance-evaluation timing or needs revision to propose the five-day range.

Confirm CMS (and any CPMS or bag-leak detection, if applicable) performance-evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria are documented in the plan per §63.628(c)(1)(iii) so that any change in timing is incorporated and available for Administrator review.

candidates.name: Phosphate Fertilizer Production (Subpart BB)

criteria.check: Confirm your operations include a 'phosphate fertilizer process line' or a 'diammonium and/or monoammonium phosphate process line' as defined in §63.621 (i.e., reactors, granulators, dryers, coolers, screens, mills associated with ammoniated phosphate production).

For each phosphate fertilizer process line, determine whether you must install, calibrate, maintain, and operate a continuous monitoring system (CMS) that (a) has ±5% accuracy over its operating range and (b) determines and permanently records the mass flow of phosphorus‑bearing material and supports a daily record of equivalent P2O5 feed calculated per §63.626(f)(3).

If using a CMS or proposing alternative monitoring parameters, confirm you can prepare a site‑specific monitoring plan with the required elements (sampling/interface location justification, equipment/specs, performance evaluation procedures and acceptance criteria, O&M, QA/QC, and recordkeeping/reporting per §63.628(c)(1)(i)-(vi)).

If you seek approval of an alternative monitoring approach (e.g., a replacement for magnetic flow meters), confirm that approval authority for requests under §63.8(f) for alternative monitoring requirements is retained by the Administrator (i.e., you must pursue EPA or delegated‑authority approval).

you_should_check: Which specific process lines at your Florida plant meet the §63.621 definitions (identify each ammoniated phosphate process line and associated equipment).

Whether your existing magnetic flow meters and associated system meet the CMS requirements (±5% accuracy, permanent mass‑flow recording, and ability to compute daily equivalent P2O5 per §63.626(f)(3)).
Whether your proposed alternative method can be documented in the site‑specific monitoring plan elements listed in §63.628(c)(1)(i)‑(vi) and support the required performance evaluations (§63.626(h)).

Whether you will need to submit a formal request for alternative monitoring to the Administrator (per §63.632(b)(3)) and be prepared to supply the site‑specific monitoring plan and performance evaluation data for approval.

candidates.name: Catalytic Cracking Units (Subpart UUU)

criteria.check: Determine whether your catalytic cracking unit is subject to the emission limitations and option choices in Table 1 of Subpart UUU (i.e., whether the unit must meet the Subpart UUU PM/Ni/HAP limits or may elect among the options listed).

If your unit uses a wet scrubber as the control device, determine which continuous parameter(s) from Table 2 you currently use or may elect to monitor and note that you must provide notice to the Administrator if you elect to change the monitoring option.

If you want alternative monitoring for a wet scrubber, check that you meet all three conditions in 63.1573(g)(1): the FCCU regenerator vent is subject to the NSPS PM limit in 40 CFR 60.102(a)(1) and uses a wet scrubber, you have Administrator-approved alternative monitoring under 40 CFR 60.105(a)(1), and this Subpart requires a CEMS/COMS for the same regenerator vent.

If you propose to monitor alternative parameters (change parametric limits), prepare and submit a request to the Administrator that includes: affected-source description and justification for the parameter, methods to demonstrate the parameter determines continuous compliance, monitoring/recording/reporting frequency, supporting calculations, and averaging time.

Ensure any continuous parameter monitoring system used for the wet scrubber meets Subpart UUU CMS requirements for installation, operation, maintenance, minimum sampling frequency (one cycle per 15 minutes), valid hourly/data-availability criteria, averaging, and recordkeeping.

Confirm that you must submit your operation, maintenance, and monitoring (OM&M) plan (and any changes) to your permitting authority for review and approval and operate according to the plan until the permitting authority approves changes.

you_should_check: Confirm the affected unit is a catalytic cracking unit (FCCU) and whether the regenerator vent is controlled by a wet scrubber.
Confirm whether the FCCU regenerator vent is subject to the NSPS PM limit in 40 CFR 60.102(a)(1) and whether you already have Administrator‑approved alternative monitoring under NSPS 60.105(a)(1).
Confirm which continuous parameter(s) or COMS/CEMS are currently required/installed for the regenerator vent under Subpart UUU and whether you plan to replace or revise those parameters.
Prepare the Administrator request contents per 63.1573(f) and be ready to submit revised OM&M plan and obtain permitting‑authority approval per 63.1574(f)(1).

candidates.name: Steel pickling/HCl (Subpart CCC)

criteria.check: If you use a wet scrubber, the rule requires installation, operation, and maintenance of systems to measure and record the scrubber makeup water flow rate (and recirculation flow rate, if applicable) continuously and record at least once per shift while scrubber is operating.

Performance testing must establish site‑specific operating parameter values for minimum scrubber makeup water flow rate (and minimum recirculation flow rate if applicable) using monitoring values averaged from test runs with measurements at least every 15 minutes.
Each monitoring device must be certified by the manufacturer to be accurate within 5 percent and calibrated per the manufacturer's instructions at least annually.
You may develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements (e.g., a conductivity‑based approach) only subject to approval by the Administrator.

you_should_check: Whether your facility is a steel pickling facility subject to Subpart CCC
Whether your emission control is a wet scrubber used to meet Subpart CCC standards
Whether your performance test(s) have established minimum makeup water (and recirculation) flow rates and the test monitoring records (15‑minute averages) that define those minima
Whether you will seek Administrator approval for an alternative monitoring approach and can meet manufacturer accuracy/calibration requirements

candidates.name: CMS requirements and alternative monitoring requests (Subpart NNNNN)

criteria.check: A required CMS must operate and collect data whenever the process is operating, collect data from at least four equally spaced periods each hour, and must have valid data for at least 75 percent of operating hours in a 24‑hour period.

For hours with ≥4 valid periods calculate an hourly average using all valid data (or ≥1 value/minute if sampled more frequently) and calculate the daily average using all hourly averages for the 24‑hour period.

For scrubber control devices you may request approval (per §63.8(f)) to monitor parameters other than those specified, but you must submit a monitoring plan and conduct monitoring in accordance with the approved plan.

The monitoring plan must identify the operating parameter to be monitored, explain why that parameter (e.g., conductivity) is appropriate to ensure control efficiency, and identify the specific monitoring procedures to be used.

you_should_check: Whether your source is subject to Subpart NNNNN monitoring requirements
Whether you will request approval to monitor conductivity instead of makeup water flow for the scrubber
Prepare and submit a site‑specific monitoring plan that identifies the parameter, justification, and procedures (per 63.9025(b)(1)‑(3))
Whether your CMS/data collection scheme can meet the four‑period‑per‑hour, ≥75% valid hours, hourly and daily averaging requirements

candidates.name: Process vent scrubber monitoring (Subpart G)

criteria.check: Where a scrubber is used with an incinerator, boiler, or process heater for halogenated vent streams, a pH monitoring device with a continuous recorder must be installed to monitor scrubber effluent pH.
A flow meter with a continuous recorder must be located at the scrubber influent for liquid flow (and gas flow rate must be determined by one of the specified methods).

Monitoring equipment must be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to the manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures that provide adequate assurance of accurate monitoring.

you_should_check: Whether you have a process vent that uses a combustion device (incinerator, boiler, or process heater) and a scrubber for halogenated vent streams subject to Subpart G
Whether pH continuous monitoring and a liquid influent flow meter are required at your scrubber
Whether your monitoring equipment will be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated per manufacturer specifications

candidates.name: General monitoring for control/recovery devices (Subpart SS)

criteria.check: This section applies if you are an owner/operator of a regulated source required to monitor under Subpart SS.
The Administrator may specify/approve minor changes in monitoring methodology or approve alternatives to monitoring requirements and procedures.
All CPMS must be installed, operational, and data verified as specified in this subpart prior to or in conjunction with conducting performance tests.

You must establish a range for monitored parameters that indicates proper operation of the control device; the range may be based on a prior performance test meeting the referenced performance‑test specifications.

you_should_check: Whether your source is regulated under Subpart SS and thus subject to these general monitoring rules
Whether you will seek Administrator approval for an alternative monitoring method under this subpart
Whether required CPMS will be installed, operational, and verified prior to or with performance testing
Whether you will establish parameter operating ranges based on performance test results

candidates.name: Process Vents (Subpart HHHHHHH)

criteria.check: Is the absorber/acid gas scrubber being used to meet emission limits for process vents in this subpart and required to have CPMS as referenced in this section?
Does the subpart require installation and operation of pressure gauges at the inlet and outlet of the absorber or acid gas scrubber to monitor pressure drop through the scrubber?
Does the subpart allow you to propose alternative monitoring parameters or procedures (i.e., request substitution of a different parameter for the specified CPMS)?

If CPMS are required, does your proposed alternative monitoring plan meet the CPMS requirements: prepare a site-specific monitoring plan, record data at least every 15 minutes, conduct initial and periodic site-specific performance evaluations, and ensure monitoring range extends ≥20% beyond normal expected operating range?

you_should_check: Whether the second scrubber controls a process vent that must meet the process-vent emission limits in Subpart HHHHHHH
Whether §63.11925(c)-required CPMS applies to that scrubber (i.e., CPMS obligation exists)
Whether current monitoring on that scrubber already has inlet/outlet pressure gauges and measured outlet pressure data
Availability of performance-test data and rationale showing ambient pressure as an equivalent parameter and the normal operating range to demonstrate the 20% margin requirement

candidates.name: Control and Recovery Devices (Subpart SS)

criteria.check: Is the owner/operator of this regulated source required to monitor under Subpart SS (i.e., is the scrubber a control or recovery device regulated by this subpart)?

Are CPMS to be installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated per manufacturer specifications, installed and operational (with verification) prior to or in conjunction with performance tests, and sited to obtain representative measurements?
Will the CPMS be in continuous operation when emissions are routed to the monitored device except for allowed short interruptions (repairs, checks)?
Can you request Administrator approval to monitor a different parameter than those listed (i.e., request approval to substitute ambient pressure for measured outlet pressure)?

you_should_check: Whether the PVC facility’s scrubber is covered by Subpart SS monitoring obligations
Whether current CPMS installation and calibration follow manufacturer specs and are verified operational
Whether you have documentation/rationale (engineering/ performance-test basis) to support ambient pressure as an alternative monitoring parameter
Whether continuous operation and representative measurement requirements can be met using the alternative parameter

candidates.name: Process Vent Monitoring (Subpart G)

criteria.check: If the scrubber is used with an incinerator/combustion device to meet the referenced requirements, does the rule require a pH monitoring device with continuous recorder for the scrubber effluent?

Does the rule require a liquid flow meter at the scrubber influent and specify acceptable methods to determine gas flow (design blower capacity with adjustments, measurement at inlet, or use of representative prior test results)?
May you request approval to monitor parameters other than those listed in this section (i.e., request to monitor a different parameter than the ones specified)?

you_should_check: Whether the process vent and scrubber fall under the applicability of §63.114 (i.e., used to comply with the referenced §63.113 requirements)
Whether you are already required to monitor pH and liquid/gas flow for this scrubber or instead seeking an alternative to the prescribed parameters
Which gas-flow determination method (A, B, or C) was used or will be used during performance testing and whether that supports an alternative monitoring approach
Whether prior approvals or performance-test data exist that demonstrate equivalence for the alternative parameter

candidates.name: Acrylonitrile polymerization and monomer recovery (PAN fibers)

criteria.check: Whether AN-containing gases from polymerization and monomer recovery equipment are collected by capture/enclosure systems and routed via a closed vent system to a control device.
If a wet scrubber controls polymerization process equipment, whether the daily average water flow to the wet scrubber is maintained at a minimum of 50 liters per minute.
If a wet scrubber controls monomer recovery process equipment, whether the daily average water flow to the wet scrubber is maintained at a minimum of 30 liters per minute.
Whether a CPMS is installed to measure and record wet scrubber water flow at least every 15 minutes and to determine and record the daily average flow rate.

you_should_check: Do your polymerization and monomer recovery vents collect AN and route them to the wet scrubber(s)?
Is the scrubber used for polymerization, monomer recovery, or both?
Do you have a CPMS that records liquid flow ≥ every 15 minutes and produces daily averages?
Have you performed or would you perform the required performance test(s) tied to any change in operating limits?

candidates.name: General monitoring requirements for control and recovery devices

criteria.check: Whether your facility is an owner/operator of a regulated source required to monitor under Subpart SS (i.e., whether your control or recovery devices are subject to this subpart's monitoring requirements).

Whether the Administrator approval route for alternatives to specified monitoring applies (i.e., you may request Administrator approval to use alternatives to monitoring requirements as provided in referencing subparts or paragraph (d)).
Whether CPMS and other monitoring equipment are installed, calibrated, maintained, and operated according to manufacturer's specifications or other written procedures to assure accurate monitoring.

Whether you will request approval to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring and recordkeeping provisions listed in the referenced sections of this subpart, or to monitor different parameters as allowed by paragraph (d)(2).

you_should_check: Are your scrubbers/control devices regulated under Subpart SS monitoring requirements?
Do you have written CPMS installation, calibration, and maintenance procedures consistent with manufacturer specs?
Do you plan to request Administrator approval for alternative monitoring or different parameters?
Can you document rationale and data to support an alternatives request?

candidates.name: Process vent CPMS requirements (absorbers/acid gas scrubbers)

criteria.check: Whether you must install and operate the applicable CPMS for each control device used to comply with process vent emission limits (and whether you are required to use CPMS per §63.11925(c)).

For an absorber/acid gas scrubber, whether you will install a flow meter to monitor influent liquid flow or both influent liquid flow and gas flow to determine and monitor the liquid-to-gas (L/G) ratio (using one of the specified gas flow methods).

Whether you will monitor pressure drop through the scrubber with inlet/outlet gauges, or (where applicable) use inlet gas–liquid temperature difference or specific gravity difference monitoring as allowed by this section.
If the scrubbing liquid is a reactant, whether you will install and operate one of the required devices to monitor scrubbing-liquid effluent (pH, caustic strength, or conductivity).

you_should_check: Is the scrubber used to meet process-vent emission limits that require CPMS?
Can you continuously measure influent liquid flow and either gas flow or compute L/G ratio as described?
Is the scrubber monitoring via pressure drop acceptable for your unit, or do temperature/specific gravity conditions alter the required monitor?
Is your scrubbing liquid a reactant (requiring pH/caustic/conductivity monitoring)?

candidates.name: Process vent provisions — monitoring requirements

criteria.check: If the scrubber is used with an incinerator, boiler, or process heater for halogenated vent streams, whether you will install a continuous pH monitor on the scrubber effluent and a flow meter at the scrubber influent (with gas flow determined by one of the specified methods).

If the scrubber/absorber is the final recovery device in a recovery system, whether you will install and operate a scrubbing liquid temperature monitoring device and a specific gravity monitoring device, each with a continuous recorder.
Whether you will request approval to monitor parameters other than those listed in this section by submitting the required approval request under the procedures cited.

you_should_check: Is your scrubber treating halogenated process vent streams or serving as a final recovery device in a recovery system?
Can you install continuous pH and influent liquid flow monitoring if required for halogenated streams?
Can you continuously monitor scrubbing liquid temperature and specific gravity if acting as final recovery device?
Do you intend to submit a request to monitor alternative parameters and have the procedures/data ready for that request?

candidates.name: RRRRR (dynamic wet scrubbers — taconite finished pellet handling)

criteria.check: Whether each dynamic wet scrubber is applied to meet any particulate matter emission limit in Table 1 (if so, the scrubber is subject to the fan-amperage/pressure-drop monitoring requirement and water flow monitoring per the date-specific provisions).

Whether during the particulate matter performance test you (using the required CPMS) measured and recorded scrubber water flow rate and either fan amperage or pressure drop every 15 minutes during each test run (after the applicable dates, fan amperage is required to be measured).

Whether the site-specific operating limit for fan amperage was established as the lowest average fan amperage value calculated for any individual test run (i.e., average each run and take the lowest of the three runs).

Whether you have/install/operate/maintain the CPMS required for dynamic wet scrubbers and are monitoring and recording the daily average fan amperage and scrubber water flow rate per the monitoring requirements.

you_should_check: Are the twelve dynamic wet scrubbers being used to meet a Table 1 particulate matter emission limit?
Which construction/reconstruction and start-up dates apply for each scrubber (to determine whether fan amperage or pressure drop could be used, and the applicable date-based monitoring requirement)?
Whether each scrubber was subject to the applicable initial performance test (§63.9620) and has the 15-minute CPMS data for each of three test runs to calculate per-run averages.

Whether the established operating limit for fan amperage equals the lowest average fan amperage from the performance-test runs (and whether CPMS is set up to record daily averages for continuous compliance).

candidates.name: DDD (change monitored parameter levels)

criteria.check: Whether you notify the Administrator of your desire to expand or change the control device or process operating parameter level established during performance tests.

Whether, upon Administrator approval, you will conduct additional performance tests at the proposed new operating parameter levels and obtain test results verifying that the new levels meet the applicable emission limits before operating at those levels.

you_should_check: Whether you intend to request Administrator approval to change the fan-amperage operating level to a percent-of-full-load definition.
Whether you can perform additional performance tests at the proposed new parameter levels and demonstrate compliance with the applicable emission limits as required before using the new levels.

candidates.name: Initial and periodic performance testing (primer‑surfacer/topcoat)

criteria.check: Verify the previous test was conducted using the methods and conditions specified in this subpart.
Verify that either no process or equipment changes have been made since the previous test or you can demonstrate the previous test results reliably demonstrate compliance despite any changes.
Verify that the previous test either established the required operating parameters or collected sufficient data to establish the required operating parameters.

Verify transfer efficiency for primer‑surfacer and topcoat was determined using ASTM D5066‑91 or the EPA protocol referenced in this section or that representative coatings/booths were tested as allowed by the protocol.
Verify the previous performance test was conducted under representative operating conditions for the coating operation and that records document why those conditions represented normal operation.
Confirm the periodic performance‑test requirement (retesting within 5 years of the previous performance test) and whether that timing requires a new test regardless of reusing older results.

you_should_check: Date and test report details (methods, standards cited — e.g., ASTM D5066 or EPA protocol) for the December 2004 transfer efficiency test
Whether any process or equipment changes (including booths, application equipment, capture systems, or control devices) occurred since the 2004 test
Whether the 2004 test established the operating parameters required by the subpart or included sufficient raw data to derive them
Test records documenting representative operating conditions and capture/control operating conditions (flow rates, inlet concentrations, booth selection) used during the 2004 test

candidates.name: Subpart NNNNN (scrubber monitoring)

criteria.check: Determine whether you are required by §63.9020(e) to monitor specific operating parameters under this subpart (i.e., whether this subpart applies to your source and imposes monitoring obligations).
If the scrubber is a control device subject to this subpart, confirm you may request approval under §63.8(f) to monitor parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e).

If requesting alternative parameters, ensure your monitoring plan identifies the operating parameter to be monitored, explains why it demonstrates ongoing compliance, and specifies the monitoring procedures to be used.

If you use a caustic scrubber or a water scrubber to meet the emission limits in this subpart's Table 1, confirm you must keep daily average records of scrubber inlet or recirculating liquid flow and daily average scrubber effluent pH.

criteria.check: Determine whether your facility is a steel pickling facility or an acid regeneration plant subject to this subpart (this section's monitoring rules apply to those sources).

candidates.name: Ethylene Oxide Emissions Standards for Sterilization Facilities

criteria.check: Determine whether you must demonstrate continuous compliance using an EtO CEMS (required by this section unless you qualify for the <100 lb/yr alternative).
If your facility's annual EtO use is less than 100 lb/yr, determine whether you have elected the alternative (annual performance testing) instead of EtO CEMS monitoring.

If you are using EtO CEMS, verify you must install and operate an EtO CEMS on each outlet for the control system and monitor each inlet used to demonstrate compliance (with stated exception for SCV streams).

Confirm the analyzer/instrumentation has the required measurement range and sensitivity (outlet MDL requirement), is continuous with ≤1-minute averaging time, and that calibration spectra/analyte spiking use EtO gaseous cylinder standards meeting PS 19 criteria.

you_should_check: Annual facility EtO usage (is it <100 lb/yr?).
Whether you intend to demonstrate compliance via EtO CEMS or via the <100 lb/yr performance-test option.
Whether the emissions stream you will monitor is an outlet to a control system (i.e., CEMS required on each outlet).
Whether you will need combined-stream or site‑wide CEMS monitoring (which requires CEMS on each exhaust stack).

candidates.name: Monitoring Provisions for EtO CEMS

criteria.check: Verify the proposed monitoring system is a CEMS capable of measuring EtO in lb/hr (Appendix A says monitoring provisions apply to EtO CEMS that must be capable of lb/hr measurements).
Confirm installation of the EtO CEMS and any additional monitoring systems will follow §63.365 and Performance Specification 19 (PS 19) as required for EtO CEMS installation.
Confirm the EtO analyzer must be certified according to PS 19 (Appendix A requires initial certification per PS 19 section 13).

criteria.citation: Appendix A to Subpart O, 5 (5.1 and 5.2)
criteria.check: Confirm the proposed device can meet the on‑going QA/QC requirements (Procedure 7 of appendix F to part 60 and applicable part 75 QA tests, including periodic gas audits/RATAs and out‑of‑control definitions).

you_should_check: Whether the ET‑6200R U series can be certified under PS 19 (including required calibration spectra using EtO cylinder standards).
Whether the ET‑6200R U series meets continuous-monitoring performance (continuous operation, ≤1‑minute averaging) and outlet MDL requirements in §63.365(b)(5)(i).
Whether you (or vendor) can perform the initial certification, periodic gas audits, RATAs, and any recertification required after analyzer replacement per Appendix A.
Whether using the device as primary, backup (redundant or nonredundant), or temporary like‑kind replacement triggers specific certification/QA tests in Appendix A.

candidates.name: Oil and Natural Gas Production NESHAP (Subpart HH)

criteria.check: Determine whether your facility is a major or area source of HAP (Subpart HH applies to owners/operators of facilities that are major or area sources as defined in §63.761).

Confirm the facility processes, upgrades, or stores natural gas prior to the point at which natural gas enters the natural gas transmission and storage source category (i.e., is a natural gas processing plant).
If a natural gas processing plant, determine whether the affected source as defined includes the group of ancillary equipment and compressors at the plant (these are listed as affected sources).

To consider a piece of ancillary equipment or a compressor not in VHAP service (i.e., establish its process fluid percent VHAP can be reasonably expected never to exceed 10.0% by weight) you must determine percent VHAP using either Method 18 (40 CFR part 60, appendix A) or ASTM D6420-99 (2004) subject to the provisions in §63.772(a)(1)(ii)(A)–(D).

you_should_check: Is the facility a major or area HAP source and does it process natural gas/NGLs prior to transmission (to confirm Subpart HH applicability)?
Which specific gas and liquid streams contact the ancillary equipment/compressors you plan to qualify as not in VHAP service, and do you have representative samples?

For each piece of equipment, how many hours per calendar year does it operate in the suspected VHAP service (equipment-leak standards apply to pieces operating in VHAP service ≥300 hours/yr per §63.769(a))?

Which analytical method will you use (Method 18 or ASTM D6420-99), and for ASTM D6420 can you meet the ASTM target-compound list, target concentration range (150 ppb–100 ppm), and the additional calibration/continuing-check requirements in §63.772(a)(1)(ii)(A)–(D)?

candidates.name: General provisions (performance testing & notifications)

criteria.check: If a relevant standard requires performance testing, the owner/operator must perform the test within 180 days of the source's compliance date.

If you intend to assert force majeure for a delay in testing, you must notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable after you first knew (or should have known) the event may cause a delay, and the notification must occur before the performance test deadline unless the force majeure itself delayed the notice.

Your written submission must describe the force majeure event, provide a rationale attributing the testing delay to it, describe measures taken/to be taken to minimize the delay, and identify a proposed date to conduct the performance test.
Any extension of the performance test deadline for force majeure is discretionary—the Administrator will notify you in writing of approval or disapproval.

you_should_check: Which relevant standards require an initial performance test and the compliance date for each source
Date you first knew (or reasonably should have known) of the furnace malfunctions and of labor strikes
Whether you prepared and sent the written force majeure notice with event description, minimization measures, and proposed new test date before the test deadline
Records showing steps taken to minimize the delay and any communications with EPA or delegated State authority

candidates.name: Iron and Steel Foundries (NESHAP Subpart EEEEE)

criteria.check: For an iron and steel foundry, you must conduct a performance test no later than 180 calendar days after the compliance date specified in §63.7683 to demonstrate initial compliance with applicable emissions limits.

For work practice standards and O&M requirements where initial compliance is not via performance test, initial compliance demonstration is due no later than 30 calendar days after the compliance date.
If you commenced construction or reconstruction between Dec 23, 2002 and Apr 22, 2004, special initial-test deadlines may apply (alternative dates or second tests as described in §63.7(a)(2)(ix)).

you_should_check: Whether your facility is subject to Subpart EEEEE and identify the compliance date in §63.7683
Which affected units/processes require performance tests vs work-practice/O&M demonstrations and their applicable deadlines
Whether your foundry commenced construction/reconstruction in the Dec 23, 2002–Apr 22, 2004 window and whether special deadlines apply
Whether you already notified EPA/state of scheduling or delays for the required initial demonstrations

candidates.name: Metal Melting Furnaces and Foundry Operations (Subpart ZZZZZ)

criteria.check: You must conduct a performance test for each affected metal melting furnace or building subject to limits within 180 days of your compliance date and report results in your notification of compliance status.

An existing foundry may submit prior performance test results conducted within the last 5 years (using required methods) if no process changes occurred or you can demonstrate the prior test reliably demonstrates compliance, and if using prior data you must notify the Administrator of that intent within 60 days after your compliance date.

Each performance test must be conducted under conditions representative of normal operations; you may not conduct performance tests during periods of malfunction and must record process information supporting that the test conditions were normal.

Semiannual compliance reports must, for each deviation (including malfunctions), report the date, start time, duration, cause (categorized as startup, shutdown, control equipment problem, process problem, other known cause, or unknown cause), and corrective action taken.

you_should_check: Which metal melting furnaces/buildings are subject to the §63.10895 emissions and opacity limits and the compliance date for each
Whether you have prior performance test results within 5 years that meet §63.10898(a)(1)-(2) criteria and whether you submitted the 60-day notification to use them

Whether the furnace malfunctions or strikes prevented testing during normal operations (i.e., tests would have occurred during malfunction) and if process records document normal-operation conditions for any test
Records of malfunctions/strikes, corrective actions, and whether those events were reported in semiannual compliance reports as required

candidates.name: General performance testing (Subpart A)

criteria.check: Whether a relevant standard requires you to perform performance testing for the affected source (the argon stir stations).

If testing could not be done for reasons beyond your control, whether a force majeure event occurred and you provided the Administrator written notice as soon as practicable before the test deadline including a description, rationale, measures to minimize delay, and a proposed test date.
Understand that any extension of the performance test deadline for force majeure is granted at the sole discretion of the Administrator.
If you plan to conduct a performance test, whether you provided at least 60 calendar days' written notice and submitted a site-specific test plan for Administrator review if requested.

you_should_check: Which specific regulatory standard names the performance test requirement for the argon stir stations
Whether a force majeure event prevented testing and the dates you first knew of it
Whether you have given (or will give) 60 days' written notice and have a site-specific test plan ready
Whether you have documented measures and a proposed reschedule date to include in any force majeure notice

candidates.name: Extensions/waivers for compliance and testing (Subpart YY)

criteria.check: If requesting an extension for a section 112(d) standard, whether you submitted the written request no later than 12 months before the affected source's compliance date.

Whether your request for an extension includes the required contents: description of controls to be installed, a compliance schedule with milestone dates, interim emission control steps, and whether you are also requesting extension of performance testing.
That the Administrator may grant an extension of compliance based on your submitted information or other information.
Whether, if an extension is granted, you accept that the extension will specify which other requirements (for example, performance tests) the extension covers.

you_should_check: Whether the applicable standard for your argon stir stations is promulgated under section 112(d) (and the compliance date)
Prepare the full extension request package: controls description, milestone dates, interim steps, and explicit request about performance test waiver
Whether you can meet the 12‑month (or other standard-specified) submittal deadline
Be prepared for Administrator-imposed conditions if extension is granted

candidates.name: Performance test requirements (Subpart TTTTTT)

criteria.check: Whether you must conduct a performance test for each affected source within 180 days of your compliance date under this subpart.

Whether a prior performance test using the same methods was conducted within the past 5 years and either no process changes have occurred or you can demonstrate prior results reliably demonstrate compliance despite changes.

Whether the required PM test methods and sample locations apply (Method 1/1A to select ports; Methods 2/2A/2C/2F/2G for flow; Methods 3/3A/3B for molecular weight; Method 4 for moisture; Method 5 or 17 for PM) and that sampling sites must be at the outlet of the control device prior to release to the atmosphere.
Whether during testing you must operate each emission source within ±10% of normal process rate and monitor/record the process rate.

you_should_check: Whether subpart TTTTTT applies to your facility and the argon stir stations (identify the affected-source scope from the standard text)
Whether a qualifying prior PM performance test exists within 5 years and whether process changes occurred since that test
Whether the argon stir station emissions are sampled at the control device outlet and whether the baghouse configuration affects representative sampling
Normal process rates and ability to operate within ±10% and record them during any test

candidates.name: Initial compliance for large copper/other nonferrous foundries (Subpart ZZZZZZ)

criteria.check: Whether you must conduct a performance test within 180 days of compliance date because you are an existing or new source at a large copper or other nonferrous foundry subject to §63.11550(b).

Whether a prior performance test within the past 5 years exists and no process changes have been made since that test, or whether you can demonstrate to the permitting authority that prior results still reliably demonstrate compliance.

Whether you must use the specified PM test methods and place sampling sites at the outlet (for concentration standards) or at inlet and outlet (for percent-reduction standards) of the control device, and which Method(s) (1/1A; 2/2A/2C/2D/2F/2G; 3/3A/3B; 4; 5/5D or 17) apply.

If a single control device is exhausted through multiple stacks (e.g., one baghouse serving multiple units), whether you must ensure three runs by representative sampling of stacks satisfactory to the Administrator and provide data or an explanation why the chosen stack(s) are representative.

you_should_check: Whether your facility is a ‘large copper or other nonferrous foundry’ subject to §63.11550(b)
Whether the baghouse is a single control device exhausting through multiple stacks and how that affects representative stack selection for testing
Whether a qualifying performance test exists within 5 years and whether permitting authority will accept prior results
Which PM compliance approach applies (concentration at outlet vs percent reduction inlet/outlet) and corresponding sampling locations

candidates.name: HCl production NESHAP (Subpart NNNNN)

criteria.check: Determine whether your facility is an HCl production facility that produces liquid HCl product at a concentration of 30 weight percent or greater during normal operations and is located at or is part of a major source of HAP.

Confirm the control device is a caustic scrubber as defined (an add‑on device that mixes an aqueous stream or slurry containing a caustic substance with exhaust gases from an HCl process vent, HCl storage tank, or HCl transfer operation).

If you use a caustic scrubber and conduct a performance test, the minimum recirculating liquid flow rate (and the scrubber effluent pH min/max) used as operating limits must be based on values measured during that performance test.

If you propose monitoring or operating parameters other than those specified in §63.9020(e), you must request approval and submit a monitoring plan that identifies the parameter to be monitored, explains why it demonstrates ongoing compliance, and specifies the monitoring procedures.

you_should_check: Whether your operations routinely produce ≥30 wt% liquid HCl during normal operations.
Whether the plant is a major source of HAP (potential to emit ≥10 tpy single HAP or ≥25 tpy combined HAP).
That the Irgafos V-47 unit is an add‑on caustic scrubber serving HCl process vents/storage/transfer subject to this subpart.

Whether performance test data (three ≥1‑hour runs under representative/normal conditions) can demonstrate that a 65 gpm minimum recirculation rate and ≥2 wt% caustic (and the resulting effluent pH) are supported and can be included in your monitoring plan to request approval.

candidates.name: Bulk Gasoline Terminal (Subpart R)

criteria.check: If you use a thermal oxidation system for vapor processing, you must monitor temperature with a CPMS in the firebox or in the ductwork immediately downstream of the firebox before any substantial heat exchange occurs.
If you use a flare as the control device, you must install a heat-sensing device (e.g., UV beam sensor or thermocouple) in proximity to the pilot to indicate flame presence.

You may monitor an alternative operating parameter (instead of the listed parameters) only upon demonstrating to the Administrator that the alternative parameter demonstrates continuous compliance with the emission standard in § 63.422(b) or § 60.112b(a)(3)(ii).

If an alternative parameter is approved, you must operate the vapor processing system to not exceed or not go below, as appropriate, the approved alternative operating parameter value, or operation constitutes a violation of § 63.422(b)(1).

you_should_check: Whether your facility is subject to § 63.422(b)(1) (i.e., covered as a bulk gasoline terminal under Subpart R)
Which vapor processor you use (thermal oxidizer vs flare vs condenser/carbon adsorption)
Whether you can develop and substantiate to the Administrator that pilot-flame monitoring demonstrates continuous compliance with § 63.422(b)
Whether your operational procedures can ensure operation within an approved alternative operating-parameter value

candidates.name: Bulk Gasoline Terminals (Subpart BBBBBB)

criteria.check: You must conduct a performance test on the vapor processing and collection systems using the specified test methods (or approved alternatives) unless an allowed option applies.
If you use a thermal oxidation system, you must install a CPMS measuring temperature in the firebox or in ductwork immediately downstream of the firebox prior to substantial heat exchange.

As an alternative to temperature monitoring for a thermal oxidizer, you may monitor the presence of the pilot flame using a heat-sensing device that provides a positive value when the pilot is on and a negative value when off.
If pilot-flame monitoring is used, the thermal oxidation system must be equipped to automatically prevent gasoline loading operations from beginning when the pilot flame is absent.

you_should_check: Whether your facility is subject to the emission standard in item 1(b) of Table 2 to Subpart BBBBBB (i.e., is a bulk gasoline terminal covered by this subpart)
Whether you use a thermal oxidation system (vs carbon adsorption or refrigeration condenser) for vapor control
Whether an initial or recent performance test has been/will be conducted to establish monitored operating-parameter values
Whether you can provide the required automatic interlock to prevent loading when pilot is absent and the rationale/data to support the alternative monitoring parameter to the Administrator

candidates.name: Miscellaneous Process Vents (Subpart CC)

criteria.check: An owner/operator of a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent using a combustion device must install monitoring equipment depending on device type (e.g., temperature monitor for incinerators in the firebox/ductwork before substantial heat exchange).
Where a flare is used (prior to January 30, 2019), a device capable of continuously detecting the presence of a pilot flame (thermocouple, UV beam, IR sensor, etc.) is required.
You may request approval to monitor parameters other than those listed in paragraph (a) by submitting a request per the procedures specified in § 63.655(h).

You must establish a monitoring parameter range that ensures compliance with the emissions standard for each parameter you monitor and submit the information in the Notification of Compliance Status report.

you_should_check: Whether your vapor control/combustion unit is regulated as a Group 1 miscellaneous process vent subject to Subpart CC
Whether the control device is an incinerator, flare, boiler/process heater, or other combustion device
Whether the flare/use date or applicability conditions trigger the pilot-flame detection requirement (note § 63.644(a)(2) reference to pre-2019 flares)
Whether you need to submit a § 63.655(h) request to monitor an alternative parameter

candidates.name: Process Vent Provisions (Subpart G)

criteria.check: Where an incinerator is used as the combustion device for a process vent, a temperature monitoring device with a continuous recorder must be installed in the firebox or in ductwork immediately downstream of the firebox before any substantial heat exchange occurs.

Where a flare is used for a process vent, a device (e.g., thermocouple, UV beam, IR sensor) capable of continuously detecting the presence of a pilot flame is required (except as specified in § 63.108(a)).

An owner/operator of a process vent may request approval to monitor parameters other than those listed if they use a combustion device listed but seek to monitor a different parameter, per the procedures in § 63.151(f) or § 63.152(e).

You must operate the control device consistent with the minimum/maximum operating parameter value or procedure required to be monitored; operation outside that range or failure to perform required procedures constitutes a violation.

you_should_check: Whether the vapor control unit is subject to process-vent provisions in § 63.113 (i.e., your vent is regulated under Subpart G)
Whether the control device is an incinerator or a flare (which dictates temperature vs pilot-flame monitoring)
Whether you plan to request approval to monitor pilot flame instead of firebox temperature and can meet the cited approval procedures
Whether you can operate and document the control device consistently with any required operating-parameter limits or approved alternative parameter

candidates.name: Control Device and Work Practice Requirements (Subpart A)

criteria.check: Flares must be operated with a flame present at all times when emissions may be vented to them, and the presence of a flare pilot flame shall be monitored using a thermocouple or any other equivalent device to detect flame presence.
Subpart A provisions for control devices apply only to facilities covered by subparts that refer to this section (check whether the applicable subpart for your source references § 63.11).
This section contains requirements for control devices used to comply with applicable subparts; applicable subparts will specify how owners/operators using flares shall monitor these control devices.

you_should_check: Whether the applicable NESHAP subpart that covers your terminal explicitly references § 63.11 for flare control-device requirements
Whether your device is a flare (rather than a thermal oxidizer/incinerator) such that § 63.11(b)(5) flame-presence monitoring applies
Whether your proposed pilot-flame monitoring method is equivalent to a thermocouple or other device called out in § 63.11(b)(5) and can meet any subpart-specific monitoring/interlock requirements
