candidates.name: Steel pickling / acid regeneration (HCl)

criteria.check: Determine whether your facility is a steel pickling facility or an acid regeneration plant that is subject to Subpart CCC.

If the HCl control is a wet scrubber, confirm you must install, operate, and continuously monitor and record scrubber makeup water flow rate (and recirculation flow rate if required) and record at least once per shift.

If the HCl control device is not a wet scrubber (e.g., HCl bubbler), confirm you must install, operate, and maintain systems to measure and record the appropriate operating parameter(s) for that device.
Confirm that you may develop and implement alternative monitoring requirements (such as alternate operating limits) only with approval by the Administrator.

you_should_check: Whether Subpart CCC explicitly applies to your South Carolina facility (steel pickling or acid regeneration).
Exact type of HCl control device (wet scrubber vs bubbler/other) and which operating parameters are currently monitored.
Whether prior performance test data exist that establish current operating parameter values/limits.
Plan to submit an alternative-monitoring request to the permitting authority / Administrator for approval.

candidates.name: General CMS procedures / alternate scrubber parameters

criteria.check: If you use a scrubber, you may request approval (per §63.8(f)) to monitor parameters other than those in §63.9020(e) by submitting a monitoring plan that meets the requirements of this section.
Your monitoring plan must identify the operating parameter to be monitored, explain why that parameter demonstrates continued control performance, and specify the monitoring procedures.
If you install a continuous monitoring system (CMS), you must operate it and collect data whenever the process is operating and collect data at least four equally spaced periods each hour.
If your control device is not a scrubber, you must submit a site-specific monitoring plan (per §63.8(f)) that identifies the parameter, justification, and specific monitoring procedures.

you_should_check: Whether you will use a continuous monitoring system or propose non-continuous checks for the bubbler parameters (dipleg immersion depth, liquid changeout interval).
Whether the proposed monitoring plan will meet the data frequency and QA requirements in 63.9025(a) or provide justification for alternate frequency.
That the plan clearly identifies the single parameter(s) you propose (e.g., dipleg immersion depth, soak/changeout timer) and why they indicate maintained control efficiency.
Prepare supporting procedures, performance specifications, and QA/QC to include in the monitoring plan.

candidates.name: Alternative method of demonstrating compliance

criteria.check: You may request approval to use an alternative method of demonstrating compliance in your initial notification, notification of construction/reconstruction, or at any time.
If you have not previously performed testing to support the alternative, you must submit a proposed test plan; if relying on prior testing, you must submit the test results and test procedures.

You must submit a monitoring plan describing the control technique, test results verifying control performance, the operating parameter(s) to be monitored, monitoring frequency, and proposed performance specifications and QA procedures for Administrator approval.
Do not implement the alternative method of demonstrating compliance until the Administrator has granted approval.

you_should_check: Whether you will submit the alternative method request in the appropriate notification or separately, and the timeline for submission.
Whether you have existing performance-test data that demonstrate bubbler performance, or whether you must perform new testing and include a test plan.
That your monitoring plan includes the proposed alternate operating limits (dipleg depth, maximum time between liquid changeouts), measurement methods, frequency, and QA/QC.
Be prepared to wait for Administrator approval before using the alternate monitoring/operating limits.

candidates.name: General monitoring alternatives for control/recovery devices

criteria.check: Confirm whether your source is a 'regulated source' required to monitor under Subpart SS (i.e., whether Subpart SS applies to your affected source).
You may request Administrator approval to use alternatives to the continuous operating parameter monitoring and recordkeeping provisions referenced in this subpart.
You may request approval to monitor a different parameter than those listed or to set unique monitoring parameters as specified in this section.
You must establish a range for monitored parameters that indicates proper operation; that range may be based on a prior performance test or other authorized index determinations.

you_should_check: Whether Subpart SS applies to your source and whether you are otherwise required to use CPMS or specific continuous monitoring.
Whether you can justify monitoring dipleg immersion depth or liquid changeout interval as a parameter indicating proper control and propose a numeric range based on testing.
Whether you have prior performance-test data or other technical basis to set an operating range for the proposed parameter.
Plan to submit an alternative-monitoring request to the Administrator specifying the alternative parameter, justification, monitoring/recordkeeping frequency, and how the parameter range was derived.

candidates.name: Open-molding / emission-capture and control monitoring

criteria.check: Does each enclosure in your emission-capture system have a device installed to measure and record either the flow rate or the duct static pressure from the enclosure to the add-on control device?

Was the gas volumetric flow rate or duct static pressure for each enclosure monitored at least once every 15 minutes during the required emission test, and was the 3-run average established as the minimum operating limit for that enclosure?

Will the continuous parameter monitoring system complete a cycle at least once every 15 minutes, produce a minimum of four cycles per valid hour, achieve valid data for ≥90% of operating hours, and allow calculation of successive 3‑hour averages per the section?

If the add-on control device is a thermal oxidizer/RTO, will you install and operate the required combustion temperature monitor, locate and calibrate it per the tolerance/validation requirements, and use the performance-test average as the 3‑hour operating limit?

you_should_check: Whether your affected units are subject to Subpart VVVV (e.g., open-molding operations/enclosures routed to an add-on control device).
Whether emissions from each enclosure are routed to the RTO/add-on control device covered by the subpart.
Whether you plan to monitor duct static pressure (vs facial velocity) at the duct location between each enclosure and the RTO and can meet the frequency/QA requirements.
Whether you will establish operating limits from the required emission test averages (3 runs) and meet the continuous monitoring data completeness rules.

candidates.name: Monitoring alternatives for catalytic units / alternative parameters

criteria.check: Do you intend to monitor a parameter other than the parameter(s) specified in that subpart (i.e., request approval to monitor an alternative operating parameter)?
Does your request describe each affected source and the specific parameter(s) to be monitored and explain the criteria used to select those parameter(s)?

Does your request include methods and procedures to demonstrate the parameter determines continuous compliance, an operating-limit certification tied to proper control performance, and the proposed monitoring/recording frequency and rationale?
Does your request include supporting calculations and the proposed averaging time for the alternative operating parameter?

you_should_check: Whether the control device/process type in this section (catalytic units) matches your equipment or whether you are using the 'monitor other parameters' authority in this section.
Whether your planned static-pressure measurement is justified as an alternative parameter and can be supported with calculations and a demonstration plan.
Whether you can meet the required monitoring frequency, data capture, calibration and QA described for alternative parameters.
Prepare the documentation (description, demonstration methods, frequency, calculations, averaging time) required for Administrator review.

candidates.name: Alternative compliance demonstration (solvent-processing focused)

criteria.check: Are you using a control technique other than a solvent recovery system and/or solvent substitution and thus requesting approval to use an alternative method to demonstrate compliance with the emission limitations in § 63.9500(a) and (b)?

Does your submission (initial notification or at any time) include a monitoring plan describing the control technique, test results verifying control performance, appropriate operating parameters to be monitored, and the frequency of measuring/recording to establish continuous compliance?

If relying on previous testing, does your request include test results and procedures (or a proposed test plan if no prior testing) and the proposed performance specifications and QA procedures for the monitors?
Will you wait to begin use of the alternative demonstration method until after Administrator approval is granted?

you_should_check: Whether the emission limits in §63.9500(a) and (b) apply to your operations (i.e., whether this solvent-focused subpart covers your processes).
Whether you are using a control technique other than solvent recovery/solvent substitution and therefore need this alternative-compliance pathway.
Whether you have test data or will propose a test plan and can provide monitor performance specs and QA procedures.
Plan to obtain Administrator approval before implementing the alternative monitoring method.

candidates.name: Iron & steel foundry alternative CEMS monitoring (pallet cooling/shakeout)

criteria.check: Does the alternative monitoring request concern automated pallet cooling lines or automated shakeout lines at a new iron and steel foundry and the VOHAP emissions limits in § 63.7690(a)(10)?

Does your monitoring plan include a description of the control or prevention technique, the continuous monitoring system or method and operating parameters, test results demonstrating compliance, operating limit(s), and measurement/recording frequency to establish continuous compliance?
Are you submitting the alternative monitoring request in the notification of construction/reconstruction for a new source or at any time per this section?
Will you await the Administrator's approval of the monitoring plan before beginning use of the alternative monitoring method?

you_should_check: Whether your facility is a new iron & steel foundry with automated pallet cooling or shakeout lines subject to §63.7690(a)(10).
Whether the static pressure-to-RTO approach is intended to demonstrate compliance with the VOHAP limits referenced in the section.
Whether you can provide the monitoring-plan elements listed (description, parameters, test results, operating limits, frequency).
Plan timing of submission (e.g., notification of construction) and await Administrator approval before implementation.

candidates.name: General control-device and work-practice requirements (Subpart A)

criteria.check: Does the applicable subpart for your affected source expressly reference § 63.11 so that these general control-device requirements apply to your facility?

you_should_check: Whether the specific NESHAP subpart that would regulate your source incorporates §63.11 by reference.
If your proposed alternative monitoring affects control-device monitoring requirements, verify whether those control-device administrative requirements (in §63.11) apply.

candidates.name: Natural gas processing equipment leaks (Subpart HH)

criteria.check: Is the equipment located at a natural gas processing plant and does it operate in VHAP service for >=300 hours per calendar year?
Is the equipment one of the defined ancillary equipment types (pumps, pressure relief devices, sampling connections, open-ended valves/lines, valves, flanges, or other connectors)?
Does each ancillary piece of equipment and compressor have to meet the leak-detection and repair requirements of 40 CFR part 61, subpart V (i.e., Method 21-based procedures) as specified here?

Can you demonstrate that the percent VHAP content of the process fluid in the equipment never exceeds 10.0% by weight using Method 18 or ASTM D6420-99 so the piece would be considered not in VHAP service?

you_should_check: Is your Texas facility defined as a natural gas processing plant under the subpart (facility location and operations)?
Which specific pieces of equipment contact the ethylene glycol/water mixture (identify pumps, PRDs, connectors, etc.)?
How many hours per calendar year each identified piece operates in VHAP service (>=300 hr)?
Have you measured or can you demonstrate % VHAP in the process fluids (Method 18 or ASTM D6420-99) to test the 10% cutoff?

candidates.name: Alternative work practice / Method 21 substitution (Subpart A, §63.11)

criteria.check: Does the applicable subpart (here, the one requiring Method 21 monitoring for these pieces of equipment) allow the alternative work practice (optical gas imaging) in lieu of a 40 CFR part 60, appendix A-7, Method 21 monitor?
If you choose the alternative work practice, have you documented the equipment, process units, and facilities for which the alternative work practice (OGI) will be used?
If using the alternative work practice, have you chosen a monitoring frequency from Table 1 to subpart A to replace the monitoring frequency specified in the applicable subpart?
If you use the alternative work practice for detecting leaks, will you still perform an annual Method 21 screening for the regulated equipment and keep the required records?

you_should_check: Does the applicable Subpart HH requirement for your equipment explicitly require Method 21 (confirm cross-reference to Method 21 monitoring)?
Do you intend to use optical gas imaging (OGI) rather than Method 21 (visual-only inspections are not the OGI alternative specified)?
Which specific monitoring frequency from Table 1 to subpart A you would select for quarterly vs other intervals (confirm Table 1 entry applies)
Are you prepared to perform and retain one annual Method 21 screening for the equipment monitored by the alternative work practice?

candidates.name: Asphalt roofing manufacturing (Subpart LLLLL)

criteria.check: Are you an existing affected source required to conduct an initial performance test within 180 days after the compliance date specified in §63.8683?
If new, did you have to demonstrate initial compliance within 180 days after April 29, 2003 or within 180 days after startup, whichever is later?
Does this subpart require you to submit a notification of intent to conduct a performance test at least 60 calendar days before the test, pursuant to §63.7(b)(1)?
Will you need to submit a Notification of Compliance Status including performance test results before the close of business on the 60th calendar day following completion of the performance test?

you_should_check: Whether your facility is an existing or new affected source (affects deadlines in §63.8686).

Whether Subpart LLLLL's tables and provisions specifically require an initial performance test for your emission points (i.e., whether you are ‘‘required to conduct a performance test’’ under this subpart).
Planned dates for the initial performance test relative to the 60-day notification and the 180-day initial-test deadlines.
Where to submit notifications (see delegated State vs. EPA Regional Office rules in §63.9(a)(4) included in Subpart A sections).

candidates.name: Performance testing requirements (Subpart A)

criteria.check: Are you required by a relevant standard to perform performance testing and, if so, must it be done within 180 days of the compliance date (unless a waiver or extension applies)?

If a force majeure is about to occur, occurs, or has occurred that may delay testing beyond the deadline, did you notify the Administrator in writing as soon as practicable and before the performance test deadline (unless delayed notice is justified)?
Does your written submission describe the force majeure event, provide rationale for the delay, describe measures to minimize delay, and identify a proposed date for conducting the performance test?
Are you aware that approval of any extension to the performance-test deadline for force majeure is at the sole discretion of the Administrator and you must await written approval?

you_should_check: Whether the circumstances causing you to want a shorter advance notice qualify as a force majeure under §63.7(a)(4).
The earliest regulatory deadline for conducting the initial performance test (180 days) so any extension request timing is aligned.
Whether you or the Administrator expect an observer/presence during the test (affects timing/notice per §63.7(b)(1)).
Proposed alternate test date(s) and the supporting documentation describing the event and mitigation measures required by §63.7(a)(4)(ii).

candidates.name: Notification requirements (Subpart A)

criteria.check: Must you notify the Administrator in writing at least 60 calendar days before the performance test to allow review/approval of the site-specific test plan and to allow an observer to be present?

If opacity or visible emission observations are required and not concurrent with the initial performance test, must you give at least 30 days' notice for those observations (delivered with the performance-test notice or separately)?
Before State delegation, must you submit notifications to the appropriate EPA Regional Office as specified?
After State delegation, must you submit notifications to the delegated State authority and send a copy to the EPA Regional Office unless waived by the Regional Office?

you_should_check: Whether Oregon is a delegated State for these notification requirements (determines whether you submit to the State agency or EPA Regional Office).
Your planned performance-test date relative to the 60-calendar-day notification requirement and whether opacity/visible-emission observations will be required separately.
Whether you will request that the Administrator review/approve a site-specific test plan (triggers the 60-day review window in §63.7(c) and §63.9(e)).
If unforeseeable circumstances arise, be prepared to notify the Administrator as soon as practicable per §63.7(b)(2) and specify the rescheduled date.

candidates.name: Chromium electroplating and anodizing NESHAP (Subpart N)

criteria.check: Whether the affected tanks are enclosed hard chromium electroplating tanks, because §63.342(c)(2) sets the standards that apply to enclosed hard chromium tanks.
Whether each tank is a new or reconstructed affected source with initial startup after Sept 19, 2012, because new/reconstructed sources must comply immediately upon startup.
Whether an initial performance test is required (performance tests must be conducted using procedures in §63.7 and §63.344) or an exception applies (see §63.343(b)(2)).

Whether you intend to use an alternate test method and, if so, whether that method has been validated using Method 301 and will be submitted for Administrator approval, because §63.344(c)(4) allows alternate methods only with Method 301 validation and Administrator approval.

you_should_check: Confirm the tanks are hard (not decorative) chromium electroplating and are enclosed.
Confirm whether the tanks are new/reconstructed and the date of initial startup.
Confirm whether you will be required to perform an initial performance test under §63.343(b) or qualify for the wetting-agent exception.
If seeking alternate test/monitoring methods, confirm the alternative can be validated per Method 301 and be submitted for Administrator approval per §63.344(c)(4).

candidates.name: General monitoring requirements (Subpart A, §63.8)

criteria.check: Whether the requested change is a minor change in monitoring methodology, since §63.8(b)(1)(i) allows the Administrator to specify or approve minor changes in methodology for specified monitoring requirements.

Whether the requested change is an intermediate or major change or alternative to monitoring, since §63.8(b)(1)(ii) provides for Administrator approval of intermediate or major changes/alternatives to monitoring requirements.

Whether a site-specific performance evaluation test plan for the CMS must be developed and submitted to the Administrator for approval upon request, because §63.8(d)(2) requires such a plan as part of the CMS quality control program.

Whether any CMS will be operated and maintained consistent with §63.8(c) (e.g., meet §63.6(e)(1), keep routine repair parts available, and have a written startup/shutdown/malfunction plan), since CMS must be maintained per §63.8(c).

you_should_check: Determine whether the monitoring you propose is considered a CMS (continuous monitoring system) under the relevant standard.
Decide whether your proposed alternative is minor vs. intermediate/major (this affects approval pathway under §63.8(b)).
Prepare (and be ready to submit upon request) a site-specific CMS performance evaluation test plan per §63.8(d)(2).
Confirm who has approval authority (see Subpart N delegation rules) before submitting an alternative-monitoring approval request.

candidates.name: Heat exchange systems (monitoring for leaks)

criteria.check: Whether the heat exchange system cools process equipment in a chemical manufacturing process unit that meets the conditions referenced in §63.100(b)(1)–(3) (and is not excluded by §63.100(c)).

Whether the cooling‑water concentration will be determined using an EPA‑approved analytical method (part 136) sensitive to 10 ppm and whether any different sampling technique (e.g., composite sampling) would require Administrator approval as an alternative method.

Whether sampling can provide a minimum of three sets of entrance/exit samples and calculation of entrance and exit means (composite sampling must still meet the 'minimum of three sets' and averaging requirement).
Whether samples are collected at the entrance and exit points defined for the applicable heat exchange system or heat exchanger grouping (i.e., correct sample locations per system type).

you_should_check: Confirm the process unit(s) cooled by the heat exchanger meet the applicability conditions in §63.100(b)(1)–(3) (or are excluded by §63.100(c)).
Confirm which analytical method from part 136 will be used and that it is sensitive to 10 ppm.
Confirm how composite sampling would produce the required 'minimum of three sets' of entrance/exit results and the averaged entrance/exit concentrations.
Decide whether to request Administrator approval for the composite sampling technique as an alternative method under §63.104(b)(3).

candidates.name: Process vents, monitoring and performance testing (including transfer operations)

criteria.check: Whether you operate process vent(s) that use a combustion device, recovery device, or recapture device to comply with the requirements referenced in §63.113 (i.e., whether Subpart G monitoring requirements apply to your vents and control devices).

Whether you need to request approval to monitor parameters or use monitoring approaches other than those listed in §63.114 (the rule provides a process for requesting approval when you seek to monitor different parameters or use different monitoring approaches).

For Method 18 (used for vent concentration determination), whether each run must be at least 1 hour and use either an integrated sample or four grab samples taken at approximately equal intervals (i.e., whether the required method specifies integrated versus grab sampling).

For transfer/transfer‑related control device performance tests, whether each run (minimum 1 hour when applicable) must use either an integrated sample or a minimum of four grab samples (so composite sampling would need to meet these run/sample requirements or be approved as an alternative).

you_should_check: Confirm whether your facility has process vents or transfer operations subject to Subpart G (i.e., subject to the §63.113 requirements and associated testing/monitoring).
Identify which test method (e.g., Method 18, 25A, or validated Method 301) will be used for the applicable test and its sampling requirements (integrated vs. grab, run duration).

Determine whether composite sampling would satisfy the '1‑hour run / integrated or four grab samples' requirement or whether you must request approval under §63.114(c) (or the Administrator under the applicable approval authority cited in the method sections).
Prepare to document that composite sampling produces equivalent data for the required calculations (e.g., concentration averaging, percent reduction, TRE inputs) if seeking approval.

candidates.name: National Emission Standards for Primary Aluminum Reduction (Subpart LL)

criteria.check: Determine whether you operate a paste production plant that must capture and control POM and PM emissions (paste production plant control requirement).

Determine whether each pitch storage tank at your facility is required to be equipped with a control system that reduces inlet POM emissions by 95 percent or greater (existing-source pitch tank requirement).

If any pitch storage tank is a new or reconstructed source, determine whether it must be equipped with a control system designed to reduce inlet POM by 95 percent or greater (new-source pitch tank requirement).
Confirm whether the pitch storage tank POM limit provisions for existing sources in §63.843(d) carry a compliance date of October 16, 2017 for your facility.

you_should_check: Which tanks are 'pitch storage tanks' at the facility and whether they are existing vs. new/reconstructed
Whether the paste production plant and pitch tanks have installed controls already and the design/control efficiency of those systems
Whether the facility was shut down and the date of any restart (to determine restarted-source provisions)
Which specific emission limits in §63.843 or §63.844 are claimed to apply to each affected unit

candidates.name: Subpart LL — Performance testing and restart timing

criteria.check: If the pitch storage tank is an existing source that was shut down and subsequently restarted, determine whether the required initial performance test must be conducted by the 30th day following startup.

Determine whether an initial performance test was already performed within 12 months prior to the compliance date or restart that could be used to demonstrate initial compliance (use of prior performance tests).
Confirm that performance tests and monitoring will follow the site-specific test plan requirements and the general provisions referenced for Subpart LL.

you_should_check: Actual restart date of the pitch storage tank and whether it was 'restarted' after being shut down on March 31, 2016
Dates and records of any performance testing performed in the 12 months prior to the compliance date or restart
Whether you have an approved site-specific test plan and the schedule for conducting required runs

candidates.name: General Provisions — Compliance dates and startup/shutdown/malfunction requirements (Subpart A)

criteria.check: Confirm that the facility is an affected source subject to a relevant section 112 standard (and thus subject to the applicability of §63.6 unless an Administrator/President-granted extension or exemption applies).
Confirm that the compliance date for an existing source is the date established in the applicable subpart (Subpart LL) and that you must comply by that date unless an extension applies.

Determine your obligations to operate and maintain affected sources, including during startup, shutdown, and malfunction, to minimize emissions consistent with safety and good air pollution control practices.
Determine whether you have developed a written startup, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM) plan by the source's compliance date as required.

you_should_check: Whether the facility and specific units meet the definition of 'affected source' under the applicable standard
Whether an SSM plan exists and the date it was developed/implemented
Records showing operation and maintenance practices during startup/restart and any emissions during those periods
Which compliance dates in Subpart LL the facility is subject to (to tie back to §63.6(c)(1))

candidates.name: Extension of compliance and procedural requirements (Subpart YY)

criteria.check: If the relevant standard is a section 112(d) standard, determine whether you may request an extension of up to 1 additional year to install controls when such additional period is necessary for installation of controls.

Determine whether your request for an extension of compliance was (or would need to be) submitted in writing not later than 12 months before the affected source's compliance date for sources not including emission points in an emissions average.

Ensure any extension request includes a description of the controls to be installed and a compliance schedule with dates for awarding contracts/orders, initiating on-site construction/installation, completing on-site construction/installation, and achieving final compliance.
Be aware that until an extension of compliance has been granted by the Administrator under this section, the owner or operator must comply with all applicable requirements of the subpart.

you_should_check: The facility's applicable compliance date (verify whether Oct 16, 2017 is the relevant compliance date for the pitch storage tank under Subpart LL)
The date your extension request was or would be submitted relative to the 12-month-before-deadline
Prepare the required content for the request: controls description, detailed schedule, interim control steps, and any other information listed in §63.1112(a)(6)
Whether you need to request extensions for any other related requirements (e.g., performance testing) and include those in the request
